cards.question: Who is the first and chiefest being?
cards.answer: God is the first and chiefest being.

cards.question: Ought everyone to believe there is a God?
cards.answer: Everyone ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great sin and folly who do not.

cards.question: How may we know there is a God?
cards.answer: The light of nature in man and the works of God plainly declare there is a God; but his word and Spirit only do it fully and effectually for the salvation of sinners.

cards.question: What is the word of God?
cards.answer: The holy scriptures of the Old and New Testament are the word of God, and the only certain rule of faith and obedience.

cards.question: May all men make use of the holy scriptures?
cards.answer: All men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted to read, hear, and understand the holy scriptures.

cards.question: What things are chiefly contained in the holy scriptures?
cards.answer: The holy scriptures chiefly contain what man ought to believe concerning God, and what duty God requireth of man.

cards.question: What is God?
cards.answer: God is a Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth.

cards.question: Are there more gods than one?
cards.answer: There is but one only, the living and true God.

cards.question: How many persons are there in the Godhead?
cards.answer: There are three persons in the godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one God, the same in essence, equal in power and glory.

cards.question: What are the decrees of God?
cards.answer: The decrees of God are his eternal purpose according to the counsel of his will, whereby, for his own glory, he hath foreordained whatsoever comes to pass.

cards.question: How doth God execute his decrees?
cards.answer: God executeth his decrees in the works of creation and providence.

cards.question: What is the work of creation?
cards.answer: The work of creation is God’s making all things of nothing, by the word of his power, in the space of six days, and all very good.

cards.question: How did God create man?
cards.answer: God created man, male and female, after his own image, in knowledge, righteousness, and holiness, with dominion over the creatures.

cards.question: What are God’s works of providence?
cards.answer: God’s works of providence are his most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all his creatures, and all their actions.

cards.question: What special act of providence did God exercise towards man in the estate wherein he was created?
cards.answer: When God had created man, he entered into a covenant of life with him upon condition of perfect obedience; forbidding him to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, upon pain of death.

cards.question: Did our first parents continue in the estate wherein they were created?
cards.answer: Our first parents being left to the freedom of their own will, fell from the estate wherein they were created, by sinning against God.

cards.question: What is sin?
cards.answer: Sin is any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, the law of God.

cards.question: What was the sin whereby our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created?
cards.answer: The sin whereby our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created, was their eating the forbidden fruit.

cards.question: Did all mankind fall in Adam’s first transgression?
cards.answer: The covenant being made with Adam, not only for himself but for his posterity, all mankind descending from him by ordinary generation sinned in him, and fell with him in his first transgression.

cards.question: Into what estate did the fall bring mankind?
cards.answer: The fall brought mankind into an estate of sin and misery.

cards.question: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell?
cards.answer: The sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell, consists in the guilt of Adam’s first sin, the want of original righteousness, and the corruption of his whole nature, which is commonly called original sin; together with all actual transgressions which proceed from it.

cards.question: What is the misery of that estate whereinto man fell?
cards.answer: All mankind by their fall lost communion with God, are under his wrath and curse, and so made liable to all miseries in this life, to death itself, and to the pains of hell for ever.

cards.question: Did God leave all mankind to perish in the estate of sin and misery?
cards.answer: God having out of his mere good pleasure, from all eternity, elected some to everlasting life, did enter into a covenant of grace, to deliver them out of the estate of sin and misery, and to bring them into an estate of salvation by a Redeemer.

cards.question: Who is the Redeemer of God’s elect?
cards.answer: The only Redeemer of God’s elect is the Lord Jesus Christ; who, being the eternal Son of God, became man, and so was and continueth to be God and man in two distinct natures, and one person for ever.

cards.question: How did Christ, being the Son of God become man?
cards.answer: Christ the Son of God became man by taking to himself a true body, and a reasonable soul; being conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the Virgin Mary, and born of her, yet without sin.

cards.question: What offices doth Christ execute as our Redeemer?
cards.answer: Christ as our Redeemer executeth the offices of a prophet, of a priest, and of a king, both in his estate of humiliation and exaltation.

cards.question: How doth Christ execute the office of a prophet?
cards.answer: Christ executeth the office of a prophet in revealing to us, by his word and Spirit, the will of God for our salvation.

cards.question: How doth Christ execute the office of a priest?
cards.answer: Christ executeth the office of a priest in his once offering up of himself a sacrifice to satisfy divine justice and reconcile us to God, and in making continual intercession for us.

cards.question: How doth Christ execute the office of a king?
cards.answer: Christ executeth the office of a king, in subduing us to himself, in ruling, and defending us, and in restraining and conquering all his and our enemies.

cards.question: Wherein did Christ’s humiliation consist?
cards.answer: Christ’s humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low condition, made under the law, undergoing the miseries of this life, the wrath of God, and the cursed death of the cross; in being buried, and continuing under the power of death for a time.

cards.question: Wherein consisteth Christ’s exaltation?
cards.answer: Christ’s exaltation consisteth in his rising again from the dead on the third day, in ascending up into heaven, in sitting at the right hand of God the Father, and in coming to judge the world at the last day.

cards.question: How are we made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ?
cards.answer: We are made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ, by the effectual application of it to us by his Holy Spirit.

cards.question: How doth the Spirit apply to us the redemption purchased by Christ?
cards.answer: The Spirit applieth to us the redemption purchased by Christ, by working faith in us, and thereby uniting us to Christ, in our effectual calling.

cards.question: What is effectual calling?
cards.answer: Effectual calling is the work of God’s Spirit, whereby convincing us of our sin and misery, enlightening our minds in the knowledge of Christ, and renewing our wills, he doth persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ freely offered to us in the gospel.

cards.question: What benefits do they that are effectually called partake of in this life?
cards.answer: They that are effectually called do in this life partake of justification, adoption, sanctification, and the several benefits which in this life do either accompany or flow from them.

cards.question: What is justification?
cards.answer: Justification is an act of God’s free grace, wherein he pardoneth all our sins, and accepteth us as righteous in his sight, only for the righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and received by faith alone.

cards.question: What is adoption?
cards.answer: Adoption is an act of God’s free grace, whereby we are received into the number and have a right to all the privileges of the sons of God.

cards.question: What is sanctification?
cards.answer: Sanctification is the work of God’s free grace, whereby we are renewed in the whole man after the image of God, and are enabled more and more to die unto sin, and live unto righteousness.

cards.question: What are the benefits which in this life do accompany or flow from justification, adoption and sanctification?
cards.answer: The benefits which in this life do accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification, are assurance of God’s love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, and perseverance therein to the end.

cards.question: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at their death?
cards.answer: The souls of believers are at their death made perfect in holiness, and do immediately pass into glory; and their bodies being still united to Christ, do rest in their graves till the resurrection.

cards.question: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at the resurrection?
cards.answer: At the resurrection believers, being raised up in glory, shall be openly acknowledged, and acquitted in the day of judgment, and made perfectly blessed, both in soul and body, in the full enjoyment of God to all eternity.

cards.question: But what shall be done to the wicked at their death?
cards.answer: The souls of the wicked shall, at their death, be cast into the torments of hell, and their bodies lie in their graves, till the resurrection and judgment of the great day.

cards.question: What shall be done to the wicked, at the day of judgment?
cards.answer: At the day of judgment the bodies of the wicked, being raised out of their graves, shall be sentenced, together with their souls, to unspeakable torments with the devil and his angels for ever.

cards.question: What is the duty which God requireth of man?
cards.answer: The duty which God requireth of man is, obedience to his revealed will.

cards.question: What did God at first reveal to man for the rule of his obedience?
cards.answer: The rule which God at first revealed to man for his obedience, was the moral law.

cards.question: Where is the moral law summarily comprehended?
cards.answer: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the ten commandments.

cards.question: What is the sum of the ten commandments?
cards.answer: The sum of the ten commandments is, to love the Lord our God, with all our heart, with all our soul, with all our strength, and with all our mind; and our neighbour as ourselves.

cards.question: What is the preface to the ten commandments?
cards.answer: The preface to the ten commandments is in these words; I am the Lord thy God which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

cards.question: What doth the preface to the ten commandments teach us?
cards.answer: The preface to the ten commandments teacheth us that because God is the Lord, and our God and redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his commandments.

cards.question: Which is the first commandment?
cards.answer: The first commandment is, Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

cards.question: What is required in the first commandment?
cards.answer: The first commandment requireth us to know and acknowledge God to be the only true God and our God, and to worship and glorify him accordingly.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the first commandment?
cards.answer: The first commandment forbiddeth the denying, or not worshipping and glorifying the true God, as God and our God, and the giving that worship and glory to any other, which is due unto him alone.

cards.question: What are we especially taught by these words before me, in the first commandment?
cards.answer: These words before me, in the first commandment teach us, that God, who seeth all things, taketh notice of and is much displeased with the sin of having any other God.

cards.question: What is required in the second commandment?
cards.answer: The second commandment requireth the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious worship and ordinances, as God hath appointed in his word.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the second commandment?
cards.answer: The second commandment forbiddeth the worshipping of God by images or any other way not appointed in his word.

cards.question: What are the reasons annexed to the second commandment?
cards.answer: The reasons annexed to the second commandment are, God’s sovereignty over us, his propriety in us, and the zeal he hath to his own worship.

cards.question: Which is the third commandment?
cards.answer: The third commandment is, Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

cards.question: What is required in the third commandment?
cards.answer: The third commandment requireth the holy and reverent use of God’s names, titles, attributes, ordinances, word and works.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the third commandment?
cards.answer: The third commandment forbiddeth all profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes himself known.

cards.question: What is the reason annexed to the third commandment?
cards.answer: The reason annexed to the third commandment is, that however the breakers of this commandment may escape punishment from men, yet the Lord our God will not suffer them to escape his righteous judgment.

cards.question: What is required in the fourth commandment?
cards.answer: The fourth commandment requireth the keeping holy to God one whole day in seven to be a Sabbath to Himself.

cards.question: Which day of the seven hath God appointed to be the weekly Sabbath?
cards.answer: Before the resurrection of Christ, God appointed the seventh day of the week to be the weekly Sabbath; and the first day of the week ever since, to continue to the end of the world, which is the Christian Sabbath.

cards.question: How is the Sabbath to be sanctified?
cards.answer: The Sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy resting all that day, even from such worldly employments and recreations as are lawful on other days; and spending the whole time in the public and private exercises of God’s worship, except so much as is to be taken up in the works of necessity and mercy.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the fourth commandment?
cards.answer: The fourth commandment forbiddeth the omission or careless performance of the duties required, and the profaning the day by idleness, or doing that which is in itself sinful, or by unnecessary thoughts, words, or works, about worldly employments or recreations.

cards.question: What are the reasons annexed to the fourth commandment?
cards.answer: The reasons annexed to the fourth commandment, are God’s allowing us six days of the week for our own lawful employments, his challenging a special propriety in a seventh, his own example, and his blessing the Sabbath day.

cards.question: Which is the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The fifth commandment is, Honor thy father and thy mother; that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

cards.question: What is required in the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The fifth commandment requireth the preserving the honour and performing the duties belonging to every one in their several places and relations, as superiors, inferiors, or equals.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The fifth commandment forbiddeth the neglecting of, or doing any thing against the honour and duty which belongeth to every one in their several places and relations.

cards.question: What is the reason annexed to the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The reason annexed to the fifth commandment is a promise of long life and prosperity (as far as it shall serve for God’s glory, and their own good) to all such as keep this commandment.

cards.question: What is the sixth commandment?
cards.answer: The sixth commandment is, Thou shalt not kill.

cards.question: What is required in the sixth commandment?
cards.answer: The sixth commandment requireth all lawful endeavours to preserve our own life and the life of others.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the sixth commandment?
cards.answer: The sixth commandment absolutely forbiddeth the taking away of our own life, or the life of our neighbour unjustly, or whatsoever tendeth thereunto.

cards.question: Which is the seventh commandment?
cards.answer: The seventh commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.

cards.question: What is required in the seventh commandment?
cards.answer: The seventh commandment requireth the preservation of our own and our neighbour’s chastity, in heart, speech, and behavior.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the seventh commandment?
cards.answer: The seventh commandment forbiddeth all unchaste thoughts, words, and actions.

cards.question: Which is the eighth commandment?
cards.answer: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.

cards.question: What is required in the eighth commandment?
cards.answer: The eighth commandment requireth the lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of ourselves and others.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the eighth commandment?
cards.answer: The eighth commandment forbiddeth whatsoever doth or may unjustly hinder our own or our neighbour’s wealth or outward estate.

cards.question: Which is the ninth commandment?
cards.answer: The ninth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

cards.question: What is required in the ninth commandment?
cards.answer: The ninth commandment requireth the maintaining and promoting of truth between man and man, and of our own and our neighbour’s good name, especially in witness bearing.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the ninth commandment?
cards.answer: The ninth commandment forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth, or injurious to our own or our neighbour’s good name.

cards.question: Which is the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The tenth commandment is Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbour’s.

cards.question: What is required in the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The tenth commandment requireth full contentment with our own condition, with a right and charitable frame of spirit toward our neighbour, and all that is his.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The tenth commandment forbiddeth all discontentment with our own estate, envying or grieving at the good of our neighbour, and all inordinate motions and affections to anything that is his.

cards.question: Is any man able perfectly to keep the commandments of God?
cards.answer: No mere man since the fall is able in this life perfectly to keep the commandments of God, but doth daily break them in thought, word, or deed.

cards.question: Are all transgressions of the law equally heinous?
cards.answer: Some sins in themselves, and by reason of several aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.

cards.question: What doth every sin deserve?
cards.answer: Every sin deserveth God’s wrath and curse, both in this life and that which is to come.

cards.question: What doth God require of us that we may escape his wrath and curse, due to us for sin?
cards.answer: To escape the wrath and curse of God due to us for sin, God requireth of us faith in Jesus Christ, repentance unto life, with the diligent use of all the outward means whereby Christ communicateth to us the benefits of redemption.

cards.question: What is faith in Jesus Christ?
cards.answer: Faith in Jesus Christ is a saving grace, whereby we receive and rest upon him alone for salvation, as he is offered to us in the gospel.

cards.question: What is repentance unto life?
cards.answer: Repentance unto life is a saving grace, whereby a sinner, out of a true sense of his sin, and apprehension of the mercy of God in Christ, doth, with grief and hatred of his sin, turn from it unto God, with full purpose of and endeavour after new obedience.

cards.question: What are the outward means whereby Christ communicateth to us the benefits of redemption?
cards.answer: The outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicateth to us the benefits of redemption are his ordinances, especially the word, baptism, the Lord’s supper, and prayer; all which means are made effectual to the elect for salvation.

cards.question: How is the word made effectual to salvation?
cards.answer: The Spirit of God maketh the reading, but especially the preaching of the word, an effectual means of convincing and converting sinners, and of building them up in holiness and comfort through faith unto salvation.

cards.question: How is the word to be read and heard, that it may become effectual to salvation?
cards.answer: That the word may become effectual to salvation, we must attend thereunto with diligence, preparation, and prayer; receive it with faith and love, lay it up in our hearts, and practice it in our lives.

cards.question: How do baptism and the Lord’s supper become effectual means of salvation?
cards.answer: Baptism and the Lord’s supper become effectual means of salvation, not for any virtue in them, or in him that doth administer them, but only by the blessing of Christ, and the working of the Spirit in those that by faith receive them.

cards.question: What is baptism?
cards.answer: Baptism is an ordinance of the New Testament instituted by Jesus Christ, to be unto the party baptized a sign of his fellowship with him, in his death, burial, and resurrection; of his being ingrafted into him; of remission of sins; and of his giving up himself unto God through Jesus Christ, to live and walk in newness of life.

cards.question: To whom is baptism to be administered?
cards.answer: Baptism is to be administered to all those who actually profess repentance towards God, faith in and obedience to our Lord Jesus Christ, and to none other.

cards.question: Are the infants of such as are professing believers to be baptized?
cards.answer: The infants of such as are professing believers are not to be baptized, because there is neither command or example in the holy scriptures, or certain consequence from them to baptize such.

cards.question: What is the duty of such who are rightly baptized?
cards.answer: It is the duty of such who are rightly baptized to give up themselves to some particular and orderly church of Jesus Christ, that they may walk in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.

cards.question: Who are the proper subjects of this ordinance?
cards.answer: They who have been baptized upon a personal profession of their faith in Jesus Christ, and repentance from dead works.

cards.question: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord’s supper?
cards.answer: It is required of them that would worthily partake of the Lord’s supper, that they examine themselves of their knowledge to discern the Lord’s body, of their faith to feed upon him, of their repentance, love, and new obedience, lest coming unworthily they eat and drink judgment to themselves.

cards.question: What is prayer?
cards.answer: Prayer is an offering up our desires to God, by the assistance of the Holy Spirit, for things agreeable to his will, in the name of Christ, believing, with confession of our sins, and thankful acknowledgment of his mercies.

cards.question: What rule hath God given for our direction in prayer?
cards.answer: The whole word of God is of use to direct us in prayer; but the special rule of direction is that prayer which Christ taught his disciples, commonly called the Lord’s prayer.

cards.question: What doth the preface of the Lord’s prayer teach us?
cards.answer: The preface of the Lord’s prayer, which is Our Father which art in heaven, teacheth us to draw near to God with all holy reverence and confidence, as children to a father, able and ready to help us; and that we should pray with and for others.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the first petition?
cards.answer: In the first petition, which is, Hallowed be thy name, we pray that God would enable us and others to glorify him in all that whereby he maketh himself known, and that he would dispose all things to his own glory.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the second petition?
cards.answer: In the second petition, which is, Thy kingdom come, we pray that Satan’s kingdom may be destroyed, and that the kingdom of grace may be advanced ourselves and others brought into it and kept in it, and that the kingdom of glory may be hastened.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the third petition?
cards.answer: In the third petition, which is, Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven we pray that God by his grace would make us able and willing to know, obey, and submit to his will in all things, as the angels do in heaven.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the fourth petition?
cards.answer: In the fourth petition, which is, Give us this day our daily bread, we pray that of God’s free gift we may receive a competent portion of the good things of this life, and enjoy his blessing with them.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the fifth petition?
cards.answer: In the fifth petition, which is, And forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, we pray that God, for Christ’s sake, would freely pardon all our sins which we are the rather encouraged to ask because by his grace we are enabled from the heart to forgive others.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the sixth petition?
cards.answer: In the sixth petition, which is, And lead us not into temptation but deliver us from evil, we pray that God would either keep us from being tempted to sin, or support and deliver us when we are tempted.

cards.question: What is the chief end of man?
cards.answer: Man’s chief end is to glorify God and to enjoy him forever.

cards.question: Wherein do Baptism and the Lord’s Supper differ from the other ordinances of God?
cards.answer: Baptism and the Lord’s Supper differ from the other ordinances of God in that they were specially instituted by Christ to represent and apply to believers the benefits of the new covenant by visible and outward signs.

cards.question: What is the visible church?
cards.answer: The visible church is the organized society of professing believers, in all ages and places, wherein the gospel is truly preached and the ordinances of Baptism and the Lord’s Supper rightly administered.

cards.question: What is the invisible church?
cards.answer: The invisible church is the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one under Christ the head.

cards.question: What is the chief end of man?
cards.answer: Man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever.

cards.question: What rule hath God given to direct us how we may glorify and enjoy him?
cards.answer: The Word of God, which is contained in the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, is the only rule to direct us how we may glorify and enjoy him.

cards.question: What do the Scriptures principally teach?
cards.answer: The Scriptures principally teach what man is to believe concerning God, and what duty God requires of man.

cards.answer: God is a Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable, in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth.

cards.answer: There are three persons in the Godhead; the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and these three are one God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory.

cards.answer: The decrees of God are, his eternal purpose, according to the counsel of his will, whereby, for his own glory, he hath foreordained whatsoever comes to pass.

cards.answer: When God had created man, he entered into a covenant of life with him, upon condition of perfect obedience; forbidding him to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, upon pain of death.

cards.answer: The sin whereby our first parents fell from the estate wherein they were created, was their eating the forbidden fruit.

cards.answer: The covenant being made with Adam, not only for himself, but for his posterity; all mankind, descending from him by ordinary generation, sinned in him, and fell with him, in his first transgression.

cards.answer: The only Redeemer of God’s elect is the Lord Jesus Christ who, being the eternal Son of God, became man and so was, and continueth to be, God and man in two distinct natures, and one person, forever.

cards.answer: Christ, the Son of God, became man, by taking to himself a true body and a reasonable soul being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost, in the womb of the virgin Mary, and born of her yet without sin.

cards.answer: Christ, as our Redeemer, executeth the offices of a prophet, of a priest, and of a king, both in his estate of humiliation and exaltation.

cards.answer: Christ’s humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low condition made under the law undergoing the miseries of this life the wrath of God and the cursed death of the cross in being buried and continuing under the power of death for a time.

cards.question: Wherein consisteth Christ’s exaltation?
cards.answer: Christ’s exaltation consisteth in his rising again from the dead on the third day in ascending up into heaven in sitting at the right hand of God the Father and in coming to judge the world at the last day.

cards.question: How are we made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ?
cards.answer: We are made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ, by the effectual application of it to us by his Holy Spirit.

cards.question: How doth the Spirit apply to us the redemption purchased by Christ?
cards.answer: The Spirit applieth to us the redemption purchased by Christ, by working faith in us and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual calling.

cards.question: What is effectual calling?
cards.answer: Effectual calling is the work of God’s Spirit whereby, convincing us of our sin and misery enlightening our minds in the knowledge of Christ and renewing our wills he doth persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ, freely offered to us in the gospel.

cards.question: What benefits do they that are effectually called partake of in this life?
cards.answer: They that are effectually called do in this life partake of justification adoption and sanctification, and the several benefits which in this life do either accompany or flow from them.

cards.question: What is justification?
cards.answer: Justification is an act of God’s free grace, wherein he pardoneth all our sins and accepteth us as righteous in his sight only for the righteousness of Christ imputed to us and received by faith alone.

cards.question: What is adoption?
cards.answer: Adoption is an act of God’s free grace whereby we are received into the number, and have a right to all the privileges, of the sons of God.

cards.question: What is sanctification?
cards.answer: Sanctification is the work of God’s free grace whereby we are renewed in the whole man after the image of God and are enabled more and more to die unto sin, and live unto righteousness.

cards.question: What are the benefits which in this life do accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification?
cards.answer: The benefits which in this life do accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification, are, assurance of God’s love, peace of conscience joy in the Holy Ghost increase of grace and perseverance therein to the end.

cards.question: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at death?
cards.answer: The souls of believers are at their death made perfect in holiness and do immediately pass into glory and their bodies, being still united to Christ do rest in their graves till the resurrection.

cards.question: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at the resurrection?
cards.answer: At the resurrection, believers being raised up in glory shall be openly acknowledged and acquitted in the day of judgment and made perfectly blessed in the full enjoying of God to all eternity.

cards.question: What is the duty which God requireth of man?
cards.answer: The duty which God requireth of man, is obedience to his revealed will.

cards.question: What did God at first reveal to man for the rule of his obedience?
cards.answer: The rule which God at first revealed to man for his obedience, was the moral law.

cards.question: Wherein is the moral law summarily comprehended?
cards.answer: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the ten commandments.

cards.question: What is the sum of the ten commandments?
cards.answer: The sum of the ten commandments is, To love the Lord our God with all our heart, with all our soul, with all our strength, and with all our mind; and our neighbour as ourselves.

cards.question: What is the preface to the ten commandments?
cards.answer: The preface to the ten commandments is in these words, I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

cards.question: What doth the preface to the ten commandments teach us?
cards.answer: The preface to the ten commandments teacheth us, That because God is the Lord, and our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his commandments.

cards.question: Which is the first commandment?
cards.answer: The first commandment is, Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

cards.question: What is required in the first commandment?
cards.answer: The first commandment requireth us to know and acknowledge God to be the only true God, and our God; and to worship and glorify him accordingly.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the first commandment?
cards.answer: The first commandment forbiddeth the denying, or not worshipping and glorifying the true God as God, and our God; and the giving of that worship and glory to any other, which is due to him alone.

cards.question: What are we specially taught by these words, ‘before me’, in the first commandment?
cards.answer: These words, before me, in the first commandment teach us, that God, who seeth all things, taketh notice of, and is much displeased with, the sin of having any other God.

cards.question: What is required in the second commandment?
cards.answer: The second commandment requireth the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire, all such religious worship and ordinances as God hath appointed in his Word.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the second commandment?
cards.answer: The second commandment forbiddeth the worshipping of God by images, or any other way not appointed in his Word.

cards.question: What are the reasons annexed to the second commandment?
cards.answer: The reasons annexed to the second commandment are, God’s sovereignty over us, his propriety in us, and the zeal he hath to his own worship.

cards.question: Which is the third commandment?
cards.answer: The third commandment is, Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

cards.question: What is required in the third commandment?
cards.answer: The third commandment requireth the holy and reverend use of God’s names, titles, attributes, ordinances, Word, and works.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the third commandment?
cards.answer: The third commandment forbiddeth all profaning or abusing of anything whereby God maketh himself known.

cards.question: What is the reason annexed to the third commandment?
cards.answer: The reason annexed to the third commandment is, that however the breakers of this commandment may escape punishment from men, yet the Lord our God will not suffer them to escape his righteous judgment.

cards.question: What is required in the fourth commandment?
cards.answer: The fourth commandment requireth the keeping holy to God such set times as he hath appointed in his Word; expressly one whole day in seven, to be a holy sabbath to himself.

cards.question: Which day of the seven hath God appointed to be the weekly sabbath?
cards.answer: From the beginning of the world to the resurrection of Christ, God appointed the seventh day of the week to be the weekly sabbath; and the first day of the week ever since, to continue to the end of the world, which is the Christian sabbath.

cards.question: How is the sabbath to be sanctified?
cards.answer: The sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy resting all that day, even from such worldly employments and recreations as are lawful on other days; and spending the whole time in the public and private exercises of God’s worship, except so much as is to be taken up in the works of necessity and mercy.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the fourth commandment?
cards.answer: The fourth commandment forbiddeth the omission or careless performance of the duties required, and the profaning the day by idleness, or doing that which is in itself sinful, or by unnecessary thoughts, words, or works, about our worldly employments or recreations.

cards.question: What are the reasons annexed to the fourth commandment?
cards.answer: The reasons annexed to the fourth commandment are, God’s allowing us six days of the week for our own employments, his challenging a special propriety in the seventh, his own example, and his blessing the sabbath day.

cards.question: Which is the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The fifth commandment is, Honour thy father and thy mother; that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

cards.question: What is required in the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The fifth commandment requireth the preserving the honor, and performing the duties, belonging to every one in their several places and relations, as superiors, inferiors, or equals.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The fifth commandment forbiddeth the neglecting of, or doing anything against, the honor and duty which belongeth to every one in their several places and relations.

cards.question: What is the reason annexed to the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The reason annexed to the fifth commandment is, a promise of long life and prosperity (as far as it shall serve for God’s glory and their own good) to all such as keep this commandment.

cards.question: Which is the sixth commandment?
cards.answer: The sixth commandment is, Thou shalt not kill.

cards.question: What is required in the sixth commandment?
cards.answer: The sixth commandment requireth all lawful endeavors to preserve our own life, and the life of others.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the sixth commandment?
cards.answer: The sixth commandment forbiddeth the taking away of our own life, or the life of our neighbour, unjustly, or whatsoever tendeth thereunto.

cards.question: Which is the seventh commandment?
cards.answer: The seventh commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.

cards.question: What is required in the seventh commandment?
cards.answer: The seventh commandment requireth the preservation of our own and our neighbour’s chastity, in heart, speech, and behavior.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the seventh commandment?
cards.answer: The seventh commandment forbiddeth all unchaste thoughts, words, and actions.

cards.question: Which is the eighth commandment?
cards.answer: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.

cards.question: What is required in the eighth commandment?
cards.answer: The eighth commandment requireth the lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of ourselves and others.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the eighth commandment?
cards.answer: The eighth commandment forbiddeth whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our neighbour’s, wealth or outward estate.

cards.question: Which is the ninth commandment?
cards.answer: The ninth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

cards.question: What is required in the ninth commandment?
cards.answer: The ninth commandment requireth the maintaining and promoting of truth between man and man, and of our own and our neighbour’s good name, especially in witness bearing.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the ninth commandment?
cards.answer: The ninth commandment forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth, or injurious to our own, or our neighbour’s, good name.

cards.question: Which is the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The tenth commandment is, Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbour’s.

cards.question: What is required in the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The tenth commandment requireth full contentment with our own condition, with a right and charitable frame of spirit toward our neighbor, and all that is his.

cards.question: What is forbidden in the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The tenth commandment forbiddeth all discontentment with our own estate, envying or grieving at the good of our neighbor, and all inordinate motions and affections to anything that is his.

cards.question: Is any man able perfectly to keep the commandments of God?
cards.answer: No mere man, since the fall, is able in this life perfectly to keep the commandments of God, but doth daily break them in thought, word, and deed.

cards.question: Are all transgressions of the law equally heinous?
cards.answer: Some sins in themselves, and by reason of several aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.

cards.question: What doth every sin deserve?
cards.answer: Every sin deserveth God’s wrath and curse, both in this life, and that which is to come.

cards.question: What doth God require of us, that we may escape his wrath and curse, due to us for sin?
cards.answer: To escape the wrath and curse of God, due to us for sin, God requireth of us faith in Jesus Christ, repentance unto life, with the diligent use of all the outward means whereby Christ communicateth to us the benefits of redemption.

cards.question: What is faith in Jesus Christ?
cards.answer: Faith in Jesus Christ is a saving grace, whereby we receive and rest upon him alone for salvation, as he is offered to us in the gospel.

cards.question: What is repentance unto life?
cards.answer: Repentance unto life is a saving grace, whereby a sinner, out of a true sense of his sin, and apprehension of the mercy of God in Christ, doth, with grief and hatred of his sin, turn from it unto God, with full purpose of, and endeavour after, new obedience.

cards.question: What are the outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicateth to us the benefits of redemption?
cards.answer: The outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicateth to us the benefits of redemption are, his ordinances, especially the Word, sacraments, and prayer; all which are made effectual to the elect for salvation.

cards.question: How is the Word made effectual to salvation?
cards.answer: The Spirit of God maketh the reading, but especially the preaching of the Word, an effectual means of convincing and converting sinners, and of building them up in holiness and comfort, through faith, unto salvation.

cards.question: How is the Word to be read and heard, that it may become effectual to salvation?
cards.answer: That the Word may become effectual to salvation, we must attend thereunto with diligence, preparation, and prayer; receive it with faith and love, lay it up in our hearts, and practice it in our lives.

cards.question: How do the sacraments become effectual means of salvation?
cards.answer: The sacraments become effectual means of salvation, not from any virtue in them, or in him that doth administer them; but only by the blessing of Christ, and the working of his Spirit in them that by faith receive them.

cards.question: What is a sacrament?
cards.answer: A sacrament is an holy ordinance instituted by Christ; wherein, by sensible signs, Christ, and the benefits of the new covenant, are represented, sealed, and applied to believers.

cards.question: Which are the sacraments of the New Testament?
cards.answer: The sacraments of the New Testament are, Baptism, and the Lord’s Supper.

cards.question: What is Baptism?
cards.answer: Baptism is a sacrament, wherein the washing with water in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, doth signify and seal our ingrafting into Christ, and partaking of the benefits of the covenant of grace, and our engagement to be the Lord’s.

cards.question: To whom is Baptism to be administered?
cards.answer: Baptism is not to be administered to any that are out of the visible church, till they profess their faith in Christ, and obedience to him; but the infants of such as are members of the visible church are to be baptized.

cards.question: What is the Lord’s Supper?
cards.answer: The Lord’s Supper is a sacrament, wherein, by giving and receiving bread and wine, according to Christ’s appointment, his death is showed forth; and the worthy receivers are, not after a corporal and carnal manner, but by faith, made partakers of his body and blood, with all his benefits, to their spiritual nourishment, and growth in grace.

cards.question: What is required for the worthy receiving of the Lord’s Supper?
cards.answer: It is required of them that would worthily partake of the Lord’s Supper, that they examine themselves of their knowledge to discern the Lord’s body, of their faith to feed upon him, of their repentance, love, and new obedience; lest, coming unworthily, they eat and drink judgment to themselves.

cards.question: What is prayer?
cards.answer: Prayer is an offering up of our desires unto God, for things agreeable to his will, in the name of Christ, with confession of our sins, and thankful acknowledgement of his mercies.

cards.question: What rule hath God given for our direction in prayer?
cards.answer: The whole Word of God is of use to direct us in prayer; but the special rule of direction is that form of prayer which Christ taught his disciples, commonly called The Lord’s Prayer.

cards.question: What doth the preface of the Lord’s Prayer teach us?
cards.answer: The preface of the Lord’s Prayer, which is, Our Father which art in heaven, teacheth us to draw near to God with all holy reverence and confidence, as children to a father, able and ready to help us; and that we should pray with and for others.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the first petition?
cards.answer: In the first petition, which is, Hallowed be thy name, we pray, that God would enable us and others to glorify him in all that whereby he maketh himself known; and that he would dispose all things to his own glory.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the second petition?
cards.answer: In the second petition, which is, Thy kingdom come, we pray, that Satan’s kingdom may be destroyed; and that the kingdom of grace may be advanced, ourselves and others brought into it, and kept in it; and that the kingdom of glory may be hastened.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the third petition?
cards.answer: In the third petition, which is, Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven, we pray, that God, by his grace, would make us able and willing to know, obey, and submit to his will in all things, as the angels do in heaven.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the fourth petition?
cards.answer: In the fourth petition, which is, Give us this day our daily bread, we pray, that of God’s free gift we may receive a competent portion of the good things of this life, and enjoy his blessing with them.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the fifth petition?
cards.answer: In the fifth petition, which is, And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors, we pray, that God, for Christ’s sake, would freely pardon all our sins; which we are the rather encouraged to ask, because by his grace we are enabled from the heart to forgive others.

cards.question: What do we pray for in the sixth petition?
cards.answer: In the sixth petition, which is, And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil, we pray, that God would either keep us from being tempted to sin, or support and deliver us when we are tempted.

cards.question: What is the chief and highest end of man?
cards.answer: Man’s chief and highest end is to glorify God, and fully to enjoy him forever.

cards.question: How doth it appear that there is a God?
cards.answer: The very light of nature in man, and the works of God, declare plainly that there is a God; but his word and Spirit only do sufficiently and effectually reveal him unto men for their salvation.

cards.question: What is the word of God?
cards.answer: The holy scriptures of the Old and New Testaments are the word of God, the only rule of faith and obedience.

cards.question: What do the scriptures principally teach?
cards.answer: The scriptures principally teach, what man is to believe concerning God, and what duty God requires of man.

cards.question: What do the scriptures make known of God?
cards.answer: The scriptures make known what God is, the persons in the Godhead, his decrees, and the execution of his decrees.

cards.question: What is God?
cards.answer: God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

cards.question: Are there more Gods than one?
cards.answer: There is but one only, the living and true God.

cards.question: How many persons are there in the Godhead?
cards.answer: There be three persons in the Godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; and these three are one true, eternal God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory; although distinguished by their personal properties.

cards.question: What are the personal properties of the three persons in the Godhead?
cards.answer: It is proper to the Father to beget the Son, and to the Son to be begotten of the Father, and to the Holy Ghost to proceed from the Father and the Son from all eternity.

cards.question: How doth it appear that the Son and the Holy Ghost are God equal with the Father?
cards.answer: The scriptures manifest that the Son and the Holy Ghost are God equal with the Father, ascribing unto them such names, attributes, works, and worship, as are proper to God only.

cards.question: What are the decrees of God?
cards.answer: God’s decrees are the wise, free, and holy acts of the counsel of his will, whereby, from all eternity, he hath, for his own glory, unchangeably foreordained whatsoever comes to pass in time, especially concerning angels and men.

cards.question: How doth God execute his decrees?
cards.answer: God executeth his decrees in the works of creation and providence, according to his infallible foreknowledge, and the free and immutable counsel of his own will.

cards.question: What is the work of creation?
cards.answer: The work of creation is that wherein God did in the beginning, by the word of his power, make of nothing the world, and all things therein, for himself, within the space of six days, and all very good.

cards.question: How did God create angels?
cards.answer: God created all the angels spirits, immortal, holy, excelling in knowledge, mighty in power, to execute his commandments, and to praise his name, yet subject to change.

cards.question: What are God’s works of providence?
cards.answer: God’s works of providence are his most holy, wise, and powerful preserving and governing all his creatures; ordering them, and all their actions, to his own glory.

cards.question: What is God’s providence towards the angels?
cards.answer: God by his providence permitted some of the angels, wilfully and irrecoverably, to fall into sin and damnation, limiting and ordering that, and all their sins, to his own glory; and established the rest in holiness and happiness; employing them all, at his pleasure, in the administrations of his power, mercy, and justice.

cards.question: Did man continue in that estate wherein God at first created him?
cards.answer: Our first parents being left to the freedom of their own will, through the temptation of Satan, transgressed the commandment of God in eating the forbidden fruit; and thereby fell from the estate of innocency wherein they were created.

cards.question: Did all mankind fall in that first transgression?
cards.answer: The covenant being made with Adam as a public person, not for himself only, but for his posterity, all mankind descending from him by ordinary generation, sinned in him, and fell with him in that first transgression.

cards.question: Into what estate did the fall bring mankind?
cards.answer: The fall brought mankind into an estate of sin and misery.

cards.question: What is sin?
cards.answer: Sin is any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, any law of God, given as a rule to the reasonable creature.

cards.question: How is original sin conveyed from our first parents unto their posterity?
cards.answer: Original sin is conveyed from our first parents unto their posterity by natural generation, so as all that proceed from them in that way are conceived and born in sin.

cards.question: What misery did the fall bring upon mankind?
cards.answer: The fall brought upon mankind the loss of communion with God, his displeasure and curse; so as we are by nature children of wrath, bond slaves to Satan, and justly liable to all punishments in this world, and that which is to come.

cards.question: What are the punishments of sin in this world?
cards.answer: The punishments of sin in this world are either inward, as blindness of mind, a reprobate sense, strong delusions, hardness of heart, horror of conscience, and vile affections; or outward, as the curse of God upon the creatures for our sakes, and all other evils that befall us in our bodies, names, estates, relations, and employments; together with death itself.

cards.question: What are the punishments of sin in the world to come?
cards.answer: The punishments of sin in the world to come, are everlasting separation from the comfortable presence of God, and most grievous torments in soul and body, without intermission, in hell fire forever.

cards.question: With whom was the covenant of grace made?
cards.answer: The covenant of grace was made with Christ as the second Adam, and in him with all the elect as his seed.

cards.question: Was the covenant of grace always administered after one and the same manner?
cards.answer: The covenant of grace was not always administered after the same manner, but the administrations of it under the Old Testament were different from those under the New.

cards.question: How was the covenant of grace administered under the Old Testament?
cards.answer: The covenant of grace was administered under the Old Testament, by promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, the passover, and other types and ordinances, which did all foresignify Christ then to come, and were for that time sufficient to build up the elect in faith in the promised Messiah, by whom they then had full remission of sin, and eternal salvation.

cards.question: How is the covenant of grace administered under the New Testament?
cards.answer: Under the New Testament, when Christ the substance was exhibited, the same covenant of grace was and still is to be administered in the preaching of the word, and the administration of the sacraments of Baptism and the Lord’s Supper; in which grace and salvation are held forth in more fulness, evidence, and efficacy, to all nations.

cards.question: Who is the Mediator of the covenant of grace?
cards.answer: The only Mediator of the covenant of grace is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, of one substance and equal with the Father, in the fulness of time became man, and so was and continues to be God and man, in two entire distinct natures, and one person, forever.

cards.question: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?
cards.answer: Christ the Son of God became man, by taking to himself a true body, and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of the virgin Mary, of her substance, and born of her, yet without sin.

cards.question: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be man?
cards.answer: It was requisite that the Mediator should be man, that he might advance our nature, perform obedience to the law, suffer and make intercession for us in our nature, have a fellow feeling of our infirmities; that we might receive the adoption of sons, and have comfort and access with boldness unto the throne of grace.

cards.question: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be God and man in one person?
cards.answer: It was requisite that the Mediator, who was to reconcile God and man, should himself be both God and man, and this in one person, that the proper works of each nature might be accepted of God for us, and relied on by us, as the works of the whole person.

cards.question: Why was our Mediator called Jesus?
cards.answer: Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he saveth his people from their sins.

cards.question: Why was our Mediator called Christ?
cards.answer: Our Mediator was called Christ, because he was anointed with the Holy Ghost above measure; and so set apart, and fully furnished with all authority and ability, to execute the offices of prophet, priest, and king of his church, in the estate both of his humiliation and exaltation.

cards.question: How doth Christ execute the office of a prophet?
cards.answer: Christ executeth the office of a prophet, in his revealing to the church, in all ages, by his Spirit and word, in divers ways of administration, the whole will of God, in all things concerning their edification and salvation.

cards.question: How doth Christ execute the office of a priest?
cards.answer: Christ executeth the office of a priest, in his once offering himself a sacrifice without spot to God, to be a reconciliation for the sins of his people; and in making continual intercession for them.

cards.question: What was the estate of Christ’s humiliation?
cards.answer: The estate of Christ’s humiliation was that low condition, wherein he for our sakes, emptying himself of his glory, took upon him the form of a servant, in his conception and birth, life, death, and after his death, until his resurrection.

cards.question: How did Christ humble himself in his conception and birth?
cards.answer: Christ humbled himself in his conception and birth, in that, being from all eternity the Son of God, in the bosom of the Father, he was pleased in the fulness of time to become the son of man, made of a woman of low estate, and to be born of her; with divers circumstances of more than ordinary abasement.

cards.question: How did Christ humble himself in his life?
cards.answer: Christ humbled himself in his life, by subjecting himself to the law, which he perfectly fulfilled; and by conflicting with the indignities of the world, temptations of Satan, and infirmities in his flesh, whether common to the nature of man, or particularly accompanying that his low condition.

cards.question: Wherein consisted Christ’s humiliation after his death?
cards.answer: Christ’s humiliation after his death consisted in his being buried, and continuing in the state of the dead, and under the power of death till the third day; which hath been otherwise expressed in these words, he descended into hell.

cards.question: What was the estate of Christ’s exaltation?
cards.answer: The estate of Christ’s exaltation comprehendeth his resurrection, ascension, sitting at the right hand of the Father, and his coming again to judge the world.

cards.question: What benefits hath Christ procured by his mediation?
cards.answer: Christ, by his mediation, hath procured redemption, with all other benefits of the covenant of grace.

cards.question: How do we come to be made partakers of the benefits which Christ hath procured?
cards.answer: We are made partakers of the benefits which Christ hath procured, by the application of them unto us, which is the work especially of God the Holy Ghost.

cards.question: Who are made partakers of redemption through Christ?
cards.answer: Redemption is certainly applied, and effectually communicated, to all those for whom Christ hath purchased it; who are in time by the Holy Ghost enabled to believe in Christ according to the gospel.

cards.question: Are all they saved who hear the gospel, and live in the church?
cards.answer: All that hear the gospel, and live in the visible church, are not saved; but they only who are true members of the church invisible.

cards.question: What is the visible church?
cards.answer: The visible church is a society made up of all such as in all ages and places of the world do profess the true religion, and of their children.

cards.question: What is the invisible church?
cards.answer: The invisible church is the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one under Christ the head.

cards.question: What special benefits do the members of the invisible church enjoy by Christ?
cards.answer: The members of the invisible church by Christ enjoy union and communion with him in grace and glory.

cards.question: What is that union which the elect have with Christ?
cards.answer: The union which the elect have with Christ is the work of God’s grace, whereby they are spiritually and mystically, yet really and inseparably, joined to Christ as their head and husband; which is done in their effectual calling.

cards.question: Are the elect only effectually called?
cards.answer: All the elect, and they only, are effectually called; although others may be, and often are, outwardly called by the ministry of the word, and have some common operations of the Spirit; who, for their wilful neglect and contempt of the grace offered to them, being justly left in their unbelief, do never truly come to Jesus Christ.

cards.question: What is the communion in grace which the members of the invisible church have with Christ?
cards.answer: The communion in grace which the members of the invisible church have with Christ, is their partaking of the virtue of his mediation, in their justification, adoption, sanctification, and whatever else, in this life, manifests their union with him.

cards.question: What is justification?
cards.answer: Justification is an act of God’s free grace unto sinners, in which he pardoneth all their sins, accepteth and accounteth their persons righteous in his sight; not for any thing wrought in them, or done by them, but only for the perfect obedience and full satisfaction of Christ, by God imputed to them, and received by faith alone.

cards.question: Whence ariseth the imperfection of sanctification in believers?
cards.answer: The imperfection of sanctification in believers ariseth from the remnants of sin abiding in every part of them, and the perpetual lustings of the flesh against the spirit; whereby they are often foiled with temptations, and fall into many sins, are hindered in all their spiritual services, and their best works are imperfect and defiled in the sight of God.

cards.question: What is the communion in glory which the members of the invisible church have with Christ?
cards.answer: The communion in glory which the members of the invisible church have with Christ, is in this life, immediately after death, and at last perfected at the resurrection and day of judgment.

cards.question: Shall all men die?
cards.answer: Death being threatened as the wages of sin, it is appointed unto all men once to die; for that all have sinned.

cards.question: What shall immediately follow after the resurrection?
cards.answer: Immediately after the resurrection shall follow the general and final judgment of angels and men; the day and hour whereof no man knows, that all may watch and pray, and be ever ready for the coming of the Lord.

cards.question: What is the duty which God requireth of man?
cards.answer: The duty which God requireth of man, is obedience to his revealed will.

cards.question: What did God at first reveal unto man as the rule of his obedience?
cards.answer: The rule of obedience revealed to Adam in the estate of innocence, and to all mankind in him, besides a special command not to eat of the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, was the moral law.

cards.question: Is there any use of the moral law to man since the fall?
cards.answer: Although no man, since the fall, can attain to righteousness and life by the moral law; yet there is great use thereof, as well common to all men, as peculiar either to the unregenerate, or the regenerate.

cards.question: What particular use is there of the moral law to unregenerate men?
cards.answer: The moral law is of use to unregenerate men, to awaken their consciences to flee from wrath to come, and to drive them to Christ; or, upon their continuance in the estate and way of sin, to leave them inexcusable, and under the curse thereof.

cards.question: Where is the moral law summarily comprehended?
cards.answer: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the ten commandments, which were delivered by the voice of God upon Mount Sinai, and written by him in two tables of stone; and are recorded in the twentieth chapter of Exodus. The four first commandments containing our duty to God, and the other six our duty to man.

cards.question: What special things are we to consider in the ten commandments?
cards.answer: We are to consider, in the ten commandments, the preface, the substance of the commandments themselves, and several reasons annexed to some of them, the more to enforce them.

cards.question: What is the sum of the four commandments which contain our duty to God?
cards.answer: The sum of the four commandments containing our duty to God is, to love the Lord our God with all our heart, and with all our soul, and with all our strength, and with all our mind.

cards.question: Which is the first commandment?
cards.answer: The first commandment is, Thou shall have no other gods before me.

cards.question: Which is the third commandment?
cards.answer: The third commandment is, Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

cards.question: Why is the charge of keeping the sabbath more specially directed to governors of families, and other superiors?
cards.answer: The charge of keeping the sabbath is more specially directed to governors of families, and other superiors, because they are bound not only to keep it themselves, but to see that it be observed by all those that are under their charge; and because they are prone ofttimes to hinder them by employments of their own.

cards.question: What are the sins forbidden in the fourth commandment?
cards.answer: The sins forbidden in the fourth commandment are, all omissions of the duties required, all careless, negligent, and unprofitable performing of them, and being weary of them; all profaning the day by idleness, and doing that which is in itself sinful; and by all needless works, words, and thoughts, about our worldly employments and recreations.

cards.question: What is the sum of the six commandments which contain our duty to man?
cards.answer: The sum of the six commandments which contain our duty to man is, to love our neighbor as ourselves, and to do to others what we would have them to do to us.

cards.question: Which is the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The fifth commandment is, Honor thy father and thy mother; that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

cards.question: Who are meant by father and mother in the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: By father and mother, in the fifth commandment, are meant, not only natural parents, but all superiors in age and gifts; and especially such as, by God’s ordinance, are over us in place of authority, whether in family, church, or commonwealth.

cards.question: Why are superiors styled Father and Mother?
cards.answer: Superiors are styled Father and Mother, both to teach them in all duties toward their inferiors, like natural parents, to express love and tenderness to them, according to their several relations; and to work inferiors to a greater willingness and cheerfulness in performing their duties to their superiors, as to their parents.

cards.question: What is the general scope of the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: The general scope of the fifth commandment is, the performance of those duties which we mutually owe in our several relations, as inferiors, superiors, or equals.

cards.question: What are the sins of inferiors against their superiors?
cards.answer: The sins of inferiors against their superiors are, all neglect of the duties required toward them; envying at, contempt of, and rebellion against, their persons and places, in their lawful counsels, commands, and corrections; cursing, mocking, and all such refractory and scandalous carriage, as proves a shame and dishonor to them and their government.

cards.question: What are the duties of equals?
cards.answer: The duties of equals are, to regard the dignity and worth of each other, in giving honor to go one before another; and to rejoice in each other’s gifts and advancement, as their own.

cards.question: What are the sins of equals?
cards.answer: The sins of equals are, besides the neglect of the duties required, the undervaluing of the worth, envying the gifts, grieving at the advancement of prosperity one of another; and usurping preeminence one over another.

cards.question: What is the reason annexed to the fifth commandment, the more to enforce it?
cards.answer: The reason annexed to the fifth commandment, in these words, That thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, is an express promise of long life and prosperity, as far as it shall serve for God’s glory and their own good, to all such as keep this commandment.

cards.question: Which is the sixth commandment?
cards.answer: The sixth commandment is, Thou shalt not kill.

cards.question: Which is the seventh commandment?
cards.answer: The seventh commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.

cards.question: Which is the eighth commandment?
cards.answer: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.

cards.question: Which is the ninth commandment?
cards.answer: The ninth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.

cards.question: Which is the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The tenth commandment is, Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbor’s.

cards.question: What are the duties required in the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The duties required in the tenth commandment are, such a full contentment with our own condition, and such a charitable frame of the whole soul toward our neighbor, as that all our inward motions and affections touching him, tend unto, and further all that good which is his.

cards.question: What are the sins forbidden in the tenth commandment?
cards.answer: The sins forbidden in the tenth commandment are, discontentment with our own estate; envying and grieving at the good of our neighbor, together with all inordinate motions and affections to anything that is his.

cards.question: Is any man able perfectly to keep the commandments of God?
cards.answer: No man is able, either of himself, or by any grace received in this life, perfectly to keep the commandments of God; but doth daily break them in thought, word, and deed.

cards.question: Are all transgressions of the law of God equally heinous in themselves, and in the sight of God?
cards.answer: All transgressions of the law of God are not equally heinous; but some sins in themselves, and by reason of several aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.

cards.question: What doth every sin deserve at the hands of God?
cards.answer: Every sin, even the least, being against the sovereignty, goodness, and holiness of God, and against his righteous law, deserveth his wrath and curse, both in this life, and that which is to come; and cannot be expiated but by the blood of Christ.

cards.question: What doth God require of us, that we may escape his wrath and curse due to us by reason of the transgression of the law?
cards.answer: That we may escape the wrath and curse of God due to us by reason of the transgression of the law, he requireth of us repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ, and the diligent use of the outward means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of his mediation.

cards.question: What are the outward means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of his mediation?
cards.answer: The outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicates to his church the benefits of his mediation, are all his ordinances; especially the word, sacraments, and prayer; all which are made effectual to the elect for their salvation.

cards.question: Is the word of God to be read by all?
cards.answer: Although all are not to be permitted to read the word publicly to the congregation, yet all sorts of people are bound to read it apart by themselves, and with their families: to which end, the holy scriptures are to be translated out of the original into vulgar languages.

cards.question: By whom is the word of God to be preached?
cards.answer: The word of God is to be preached only by such as are sufficiently gifted, and also duly approved and called to that office.

cards.question: How do the sacraments become effectual means of salvation?
cards.answer: The sacraments become effectual means of salvation, not by any power in themselves, or any virtue derived from the piety or intention of him by whom they are administered, but only by the working of the Holy Ghost, and the blessing of Christ, by whom they are instituted.

cards.question: What are the parts of a sacrament?
cards.answer: The parts of a sacrament are two; the one an outward and sensible sign, used according to Christ’s own appointment; the other an inward and spiritual grace thereby signified.

cards.question: How many sacraments hath Christ instituted in his church under the New Testament?
cards.answer: Under the New Testament Christ hath instituted in his church only two sacraments, Baptism and the Lord’s supper.

cards.question: May any who profess the faith, and desire to come to the Lord’s supper, be kept from it?
cards.answer: Such as are found to be ignorant or scandalous, notwithstanding their profession of the faith, and desire to come to the Lord’s supper, may and ought to be kept from that sacrament, by the power which Christ hath left in his church, until they receive instruction, and manifest their reformation.

cards.question: Wherein do the sacraments of baptism and the Lord’s supper agree?
cards.answer: The sacraments of baptism and the Lord’s supper agree, in that the author of both is God; the spiritual part of both is Christ and his benefits; both are seals of the same covenant, are to be dispensed by ministers of the gospel, and by none other; and to be continued in the church of Christ until his second coming.

cards.question: What is prayer?
cards.answer: Prayer is an offering up of our desires unto God, in the name of Christ, by the help of his Spirit; with confession of our sins, and thankful acknowledgment of his mercies.

cards.question: Are we to pray unto God only?
cards.answer: God only being able to search the hearts, hear the requests, pardon the sins, and fulfil the desires of all; and only to be believed in, and worshiped with religious worship; prayer, which is a special part thereof, is to be made by all to him alone, and to none other.

cards.question: What is it to pray in the name of Christ?
cards.answer: To pray in the name of Christ is, in obedience to his command, and in confidence on his promises, to ask mercy for his sake; not by bare mentioning of his name, but by drawing our encouragement to pray, and our boldness, strength, and hope of acceptance in prayer, from Christ and his mediation.

cards.question: Why are we to pray in the name of Christ?
cards.answer: The sinfulness of man, and his distance from God by reason thereof, being so great, as that we can have no access into his presence without a mediator; and there being none in heaven or earth appointed to, or fit for, that glorious work but Christ alone, we are to pray in no other name but his only.

cards.question: For whom are we to pray?
cards.answer: We are to pray for the whole church of Christ upon earth; for magistrates, and ministers; for ourselves, our brethren, yea, our enemies; and for all sorts of men living, or that shall live hereafter; but not for the dead, nor for those that are known to have sinned the sin unto death.

cards.question: For what things are we to pray?
cards.answer: We are to pray for all things tending to the glory of God, the welfare of the church, our own or others good; but not for anything that is unlawful.

cards.question: How are we to pray?
cards.answer: We are to pray with an awful apprehension of the majesty of God, and deep sense of our own unworthiness, necessities, and sins; with penitent, thankful, and enlarged hearts; with understanding, faith, sincerity, fervency, love, and perseverance, waiting upon him, with humble submission to his will.

cards.question: What rule hath God given for our direction in the duty of prayer?
cards.answer: The whole word of God is of use to direct us in the duty of prayer; but the special rule of direction is that form of prayer which our Savior Christ taught his disciples, commonly called The Lord’s prayer.

cards.question: How is the Lord’s prayer to be used?
cards.answer: The Lord’s prayer is not only for direction, as a pattern, according to which we are to make other prayers; but may also be used as a prayer, so that it be done with understanding, faith, reverence, and other graces necessary to the right performance of the duty of prayer.

cards.question: Of how many parts doth the Lord’s prayer consist?
cards.answer: The Lord’s prayer consists of three parts; a preface, petitions, and a conclusion.

cards.question: What do you need to know in order to live and die in the joy of this comfort?
cards.answer: First, how great my sins and misery are; second, how I am delivered from all my sins and misery; third, how I am to be thankful to God for such deliverance.

cards.question: From where do you know your sins and misery?
cards.answer: From the law of God.

cards.question: Can you keep all this perfectly?
cards.answer: No, I am inclined by nature to hate God and my neighbour.

cards.question: Did God, then, create man so wicked and perverse?
