cards.answer: No, on the contrary, God created man good and in His image, that is, in true righteousness and holiness, so that he might rightly know God His Creator, heartily love Him, and live with Him in eternal blessedness to praise and glorify Him.

cards.question: From where, then, did man’s depraved nature come?
cards.answer: From the fall and disobedience of our first parents, Adam and Eve, in Paradise, for there our nature became so corrupt that we are all conceived and born in sin.

cards.question: But are we so corrupt that we are totally unable to do any good and inclined to all evil?
cards.answer: Yes, unless we are regenerated by the Spirit of God.

cards.question: Is God, then, not unjust by requiring in His law what man cannot do?
cards.answer: No, for God so created man that he was able to do it. But man, at the instigation of the devil, in deliberate disobedience robbed himself and all his descendants of these gifts.

cards.question: Will God allow such disobedience and apostasy to go unpunished?
cards.answer: Certainly not. He is terribly displeased with our original sin as well as our actual sins. Therefore He will punish them by a just judgment both now and eternally, as He has declared: Cursed be every one who does not abide by all things written in the book of the law, and do them (Galatians 3:10).

cards.question: But is God not also merciful?
cards.answer: God is indeed merciful, but He is also just. His justice requires that sin committed against the most high majesty of God also be punished with the most severe, that is, with everlasting, punishment of body and soul.

cards.question: Since, according to God’s righteous judgment we deserve temporal and eternal punishment, how can we escape this punishment and be again received into favour?
cards.answer: God demands that His justice be satisfied. Therefore full payment must be made either by ourselves or by another.

cards.question: Can any mere creature pay for us?
cards.answer: No. In the first place, God will not punish another creature for the sin which man has committed. Furthermore, no mere creature can sustain the burden of God’s eternal wrath against sin and deliver others from it.

cards.question: What kind of mediator and deliverer must we seek?
cards.answer: One who is a true and righteous man, and yet more powerful than all creatures; that is, one who is at the same time true God.

cards.question: Why must He be a true and righteous man?
cards.answer: He must be a true man because the justice of God requires that the same human nature which has sinned should pay for sin. He must be a righteous man because one who himself is a sinner cannot pay for others.

cards.question: Why must He at the same time be true God?
cards.answer: He must be true God so that by the power of His divine nature He might bear in His human nature the burden of God’s wrath, and might obtain for us and restore to us righteousness and life.

cards.question: But who is that Mediator who at the same time is true God and a true and righteous man?
cards.answer: Our Lord Jesus Christ, whom God made our wisdom, our righteousness and sanctification and redemption (I Corinthians 1:30).

cards.question: From where do you know this?
cards.answer: From the holy gospel, which God Himself first revealed in Paradise. Later, He had it proclaimed by the patriarchs and prophets, and foreshadowed by the sacrifices and other ceremonies of the law. Finally, He had it fulfilled through His only Son.

cards.question: Are all men, then, saved by Christ just as they perished through Adam?
cards.answer: No. Only those are saved who by a true faith are grafted into Christ and accept all His benefits.

cards.question: What, then, must a Christian believe?
cards.answer: All that is promised us in the Gospel, which the articles of our catholic and undoubted Christian faith teach us in a summary.

cards.question: Since there is only one God, why do you speak of three persons, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit?
cards.answer: Because God has so revealed Himself in His Word[2] that these three distinct persons are the one, true, eternal God.

cards.question: What do you understand by the providence of God?
cards.answer: God’s providence is His almighty and ever present power, whereby, as with His hand, He still upholds heaven and earth and all creatures, and so governs them that leaf and blade, rain and drought, fruitful and barren years, food and drink, health and sickness, riches and poverty, indeed, all things, come not by chance but by His fatherly hand.

cards.question: What does it benefit us to know that God has created all things and still upholds them by His providence?
cards.answer: We can be patient in adversity, thankful in prosperity, and with a view to the future we can have a firm confidence in our faithful God and Father that no creature shall separate us from His love; for all creatures are so completely in His hand that without His will they cannot so much as move.

cards.question: Why is the Son of God called Jesus, that is, Saviour?
cards.answer: Because He saves us from all our sins, and because salvation is not to be sought or found in anyone else.

cards.question: Do those believe in the only Saviour Jesus who seek their salvation and well-being from saints, in themselves, or anywhere else?
cards.answer: No. Though they boast of Him in words, they in fact deny the only Saviour Jesus. For one of two things must be true: either Jesus is not a complete Saviour, or those who by true faith accept this Saviour must find in Him all that is necessary for their salvation.

cards.question: Why is He called God’s only begotten Son, since we also are children of God?
cards.answer: Because Christ alone is the eternal, natural Son of God. We, however, are children of God by adoption, through grace, for Christ’s sake.

cards.question: Why do you call Him our Lord?
cards.answer: Because He has ransomed us, body and soul, from all our sins, not with silver or gold but with His precious blood, and has freed us from all the power of the devil to make us His own possession.

cards.question: What do you confess when you say: He was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the virgin Mary?
cards.answer: The eternal Son of God, who is and remains true and eternal God, took upon Himself true human nature from the flesh and blood of the virgin Mary, through the working of the Holy Spirit. Thus He is also the true seed of David, and like His brothers in every respect, yet without sin.

cards.question: What benefit do you receive from the holy conception and birth of Christ?
cards.answer: He is our Mediator, and with His innocence and perfect holiness covers, in the sight of God, my sin, in which I was conceived and born.

cards.question: Why did He suffer under Pontius Pilate as judge?
cards.answer: Though innocent, Christ was condemned by an earthly judge, and so He freed us from the severe judgment of God that was to fall on us.

cards.question: Does it have a special meaning that Christ was crucified and did not die in a different way?
cards.answer: Yes. Thereby I am assured that He took upon Himself the curse which lay on me, for a crucified one was cursed by God.

cards.question: Why was it necessary for Christ to humble Himself even unto death?
cards.answer: Because of the justice and truth of God satisfaction for our sins could be made in no other way than by the death of the Son of God.

cards.question: Why was he buried?
cards.answer: His burial testified that He had really died.

cards.question: Since Christ has died for us, why do we still have to die?
cards.answer: Our death is not a payment for our sins, but it puts an end to sin and is an entrance into eternal life.

cards.question: What further benefit do we receive from Christ’s sacrifice and death on the cross?
cards.answer: Through Christ’s death our old nature is crucified, put to death, and buried with Him, so that the evil desires of the flesh may no longer reign in us, but that we may offer ourselves to Him as a sacrifice of thankfulness.

cards.question: Why is there added: He descended into hell?
cards.answer: In my greatest sorrows and temptations I may be assured and comforted that my Lord Jesus Christ, by His unspeakable anguish, pain, terror, and agony, which He endured throughout all His sufferings but especially on the cross, has delivered me from the anguish and torment of hell.

cards.question: How does Christ’s resurrection benefit us?
cards.answer: First, by His resurrection He has overcome death, so that He could make us share in the righteousness which He had obtained for us by His death. Second, by His power we too are raised up to a new life. Third, Christ’s resurrection is to us a sure pledge of our glorious resurrection.

cards.question: What do you confess when you say, He ascended into heaven?
cards.answer: That Christ, before the eyes of His disciples, was taken up from the earth into heaven, and that He is there for our benefit until He comes again to judge the living and the dead.

cards.question: Is Christ, then, not with us until the end of the world, as He has promised us?
cards.answer: Christ is true man and true God. With respect to His human nature He is no longer on earth,[2] but with respect to His divinity, majesty, grace, and Spirit He is never absent from us.[3]

cards.question: But are the two natures in Christ not separated from each other if His human nature is not present wherever His divinity is?
cards.answer: Not at all, for His divinity has no limits and is present everywhere. So it must follow that His divinity is indeed beyond the human nature which He has taken on and nevertheless is within this human nature and remains personally united with it.

cards.question: Why is it added, And sits at the right hand of God?
cards.answer: Christ ascended into heaven to manifest Himself there as Head of His Church, through whom the Father governs all things.

cards.question: How does the glory of Christ, our Head, benefit us?
cards.answer: First, by His Holy Spirit He pours out heavenly gifts upon us, His members. Second, by His power He defends and preserves us against all enemies.

cards.question: What do you believe concerning the Holy Spirit?
cards.answer: First, He is, together with the Father and the Son, true and eternal God. Second, He is also given to me, to make me by true faith share in Christ and all His benefits, to comfort me, and to remain with me forever.

cards.question: What do you understand by the communion of saints?
cards.answer: First, that believers, all and everyone, as members of Christ have communion with Him and share in all His treasures and gifts. Second, that everyone is duty-bound to use his gifts readily and cheerfully for the benefit and well-being of the other members.

cards.question: What do you believe concerning the forgiveness of sins?
cards.answer: I believe that God, because of Christ’s satisfaction, will no more remember my sins, nor my sinful nature, against which I have to struggle all my life, but He will graciously grant me the righteousness of Christ, that I may never come into condemnation.

cards.question: What comfort does the resurrection of the body offer you?
cards.answer: Not only shall my soul after this life immediately be taken up to Christ, my Head, but also this my flesh, raised by the power of Christ, shall be reunited with my soul and made like Christ’s glorious body.

cards.question: What comfort do you receive from the article about the life everlasting?
cards.answer: Since I now already feel in my heart the beginning of eternal joy, I shall after this life possess perfect blessedness, such as no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor the heart of man conceived—a blessedness in which to praise God forever.

cards.question: Why do you say that you are righteous only by faith?
cards.answer: Not that I am acceptable to God on account of the worthiness of my faith, for only the satisfaction, righteousness, and holiness of Christ is my righteousness before God. I can receive this righteousness and make it mine my own by faith only.

cards.question: But why can our good works not be our righteousness before God, or at least a part of it?
cards.answer: Because the righteousness which can stand before God’s judgment must be absolutely perfect and in complete agreement with the law of God, whereas even our best works in this life are all imperfect and defiled with sin.

cards.question: But do our good works earn nothing, even though God promises to reward them in this life and the next?
cards.answer: This reward is not earned ; it is a gift of grace.

cards.question: Does this teaching not make people careless and wicked?
cards.answer: No. It is impossible that those grafted into Christ by true faith should not bring forth fruits of thankfulness.

cards.question: Since then faith alone makes us share in Christ and all His benefits, where does this faith come from?
cards.answer: From the Holy Spirit, who works it in our hearts by the preaching of the gospel, and strengthens it by the use of the sacraments.

cards.question: What are the sacraments?
cards.answer: The sacraments are holy, visible signs and seals. They were instituted by God so that by their use He might the more fully declare and seal to us the promise of the gospel. And this is the promise: that God graciously grants us forgiveness of sins and everlasting life because of the one sacrifice of Christ accomplished on the cross.

cards.question: Are both the Word and the sacraments then intended to focus our faith on the sacrifice of Jesus Christ on the cross as the only ground of our salvation?
cards.answer: Yes, indeed. The Holy Spirit teaches us in the gospel and assures us by the sacraments that our entire salvation rests on Christ’s one sacrifice for us on the cross.

cards.question: How many sacraments has Christ instituted in the new covenant?
cards.answer: Two: holy baptism and the holy supper.

cards.question: How does holy baptism signify and seal to you that the one sacrifice of Christ on the cross benefits you?
cards.answer: In this way: Christ instituted this outward washing and with it gave the promise that, as surely as water washes away the dirt from the body, so certainly His blood and Spirit wash away the impurity of my soul, that is, all my sins.

cards.question: Does this outward washing with water itself wash away sins?
cards.answer: No, only the blood of Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit cleanse us from all sins.

cards.question: Are those also to be admitted to the Lord’s supper who by their confession and life show that they are unbelieving and ungodly?
cards.answer: No, for then the covenant of God would be profaned and His wrath kindled against the whole congregation. Therefore, according to the command of Christ and His apostles, the Christian church is duty-bound to exclude such persons by the keys of the kingdom of heaven, until they amend their lives.

cards.question: What are the keys of the kingdom of heaven?
cards.answer: The preaching of the holy gospel and church discipline. By these two the kingdom of heaven is opened to believers and closed to unbelievers.

cards.question: Can those be saved who do not turn to God from their ungrateful and impenitent walk of life?
cards.answer: By no means. Scripture says that no unchaste person, idolater, adulterer, thief, greedy person, drunkard, slanderer, robber, or the like shall inherit the kingdom of God.

cards.question: What is the true repentance or conversion of man?
cards.answer: It is the dying of the old nature and the coming to life of the new.

cards.question: What is the dying of the old nature?
cards.answer: It is to grieve with heartfelt sorrow that we have offended God by our sin, and more and more to hate it and flee from it.

cards.question: What is the coming to life of the new nature?
cards.answer: It is a heartfelt joy in God through Christ, and a love and delight to live according to the will of God in all good works.

cards.question: But what are good works?
cards.answer: Only those which are done out of true faith, in accordance with the law of God, and to His glory, and not those based on our own opinion or on precepts of men.

cards.question: How are these commandments divided?
cards.answer: Into two parts. The first teaches us how to live in relation to God; the second, what duties we owe our neighbour.

cards.question: What is idolatry?
cards.answer: Idolatry is having or inventing something in which to put our trust instead of, or in addition to, the only true God who has revealed Himself in His Word.

cards.question: What does God require in the second commandment?
cards.answer: We are not to make an image of God in any way, nor to worship Him in any other manner than He has commanded in His Word.

cards.question: May we then not make any image at all?
cards.answer: God cannot and may not be visibly portrayed in any way. Creatures may be portrayed, but God forbids us to make or have any images of them in order to worship them or to serve God through them.

cards.question: But may images not be tolerated in the churches as “books for the laity”?
cards.answer: No, for we should not be wiser than God. He wants His people to be taught not by means of dumb images but by the living preaching of His Word.

cards.question: Is the blaspheming of God’s Name by swearing and cursing such a grievous sin that God is angry also with those who do not prevent and forbid it as much as they can?
cards.answer: Certainly, for no sin is greater or provokes God’s wrath more than the blaspheming of His Name. That is why He commanded it to be punished with death.

cards.question: But may we swear an oath by the Name of God in a godly manner?
cards.answer: Yes, when the government demands it of its subjects, or when necessity requires it, in order to maintain and promote fidelity and truth, to God’s glory and for our neighbour’s good. Such oath-taking is based on God’s Word and was therefore rightly used by saints in the Old and the New Testament.

cards.question: May we also swear by saints or other creatures?
cards.answer: No. A lawful oath is a calling upon God, who alone knows the heart, to bear witness to the truth, and to punish me if I swear falsely. No creature is worthy of such honour.

cards.question: What does God require in the fifth commandment?
cards.answer: That I show all honour, love, and faithfulness to my father and mother and to all those in authority over me, submit myself with due obedience to their good instruction and discipline, and also have patience with their weaknesses and shortcomings, since it is God’s will to govern us by their hand.

cards.question: What does God require in the sixth commandment?
cards.answer: I am not to dishonour, hate, injure, or kill my neighbour by thoughts, words, or gestures, and much less by deeds, whether personally or through another; rather, I am to put away all desire of revenge. Moreover, I am not to harm or recklessly endanger myself. Therefore, also, the government bears the sword to prevent murder.

cards.question: What does the seventh commandment teach us?
cards.answer: That all unchastity is cursed by God. We must therefore detest it from the heart and live chaste and disciplined lives, both within and outside of holy marriage.

cards.question: Does God in this commandment forbid nothing more than adultery and similar shameful sins?
cards.answer: Since we, body and soul, are temples of the Holy Spirit, it is God’s will that we keep ourselves pure and holy. Therefore He forbids all unchaste acts, gestures, words, thoughts, desires, and whatever may entice us to unchastity.

cards.question: What does God forbid in the eighth commandment?
cards.answer: God forbids not only outright theft and robbery but also such wicked schemes and devices as false weights and measures, deceptive merchandising, counterfeit money, and usury; we must not defraud our neighbour in any way, whether by force or by show of right. In addition God forbids all greed and all abuse or squandering of His gifts.

cards.question: What does the tenth commandment require of us?
cards.answer: That not even the slightest thought or desire contrary to any of God’s commandments should ever arise in our heart. Rather, we should always hate all sin with all our heart, and delight in all righteousness.

cards.question: But can those converted to God keep these commandments perfectly?
cards.answer: No. In this life even the holiest have only a small beginning of this obedience. Nevertheless, with earnest purpose they do begin to live not only according to some but to all the commandments of God.

cards.question: Why is prayer necessary for Christians?
cards.answer: Because prayer is the most important part of the thankfulness which God requires of us. Moreover, God will give His grace and the Holy Spirit only to those who constantly and with heartfelt longing ask Him for these gifts and thank Him for them.

cards.question: What has God commanded us to ask of Him?
cards.answer: All the things we need for body and soul, as included in the prayer which Christ our Lord Himself taught us.

cards.question: Why has Christ commanded us to address God as Our Father?
cards.answer: To awaken in us at the very beginning of our prayer that childlike reverence and trust toward God which should be basic to our prayer: God has become our Father through Christ and will much less deny us what we ask of Him in faith than our fathers would refuse us earthly things.

cards.question: Why is there added, Who art in heaven?
cards.answer: These words teach us not to think of God’s heavenly majesty in an earthly manner, and to expect from His almighty power all things we need for body and soul.

cards.question: What is the third petition?
cards.answer: Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. That is: Grant that we and all men may deny our own will, and without any murmuring obey Thy will, for it alone is good. Grant also that everyone may carry out the duties of his office and calling as willingly and faithfully as the angels in heaven.

cards.question: What is the fifth petition?
cards.answer: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. That is: For the sake of Christ’s blood, do not impute to us, wretched sinners; any of our transgressions, nor the evil which still clings to us, as we also find this evidence of Thy grace in us that we are fully determined wholeheartedly to forgive our neighbor.

cards.question: How do you conclude your prayer?
cards.answer: For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. That is: All this we ask of Thee because, as our King, having power over all things, Thou art both willing and able to give us all that is good, and because not we but Thy holy Name should so receive all glory for ever.

cards.question: What does the word Amen mean?
cards.answer: Amen means: It is true and certain. For God has much more certainly heard my prayer than I feel in my heart that I desire this of Him.

cards.question: How many things are necessary for thee to know, that thou injoying this comfort mayst live and dye happily?
cards.answer: Three. The first, what is the greatness of my sin and misery. The second, how I am delivered from all Sin and Misery. The third, what thanks I owe unto God for this delivery.

cards.question: Whence knowest thou thy misery?
cards.answer: Out of the Law of God.

cards.question: Did God then make man so wicked and perverse?
cards.answer: Not so, but rather he made him good, and to his own Image; that is, indued with true Righteousness and Holiness, that he might rightly know God his Creator, and heartily love him, and live with him blessed for ever, and that to laud and magnify him.

cards.question: Whence then ariseth the wickedness of Mans nature?
cards.answer: From the fall and disobedience of our first Parents Adam and Eve: hence is our nature so corrupt that we are all conceived and born in Sin.

cards.question: Are we so corrupt that we are not at all apt to do well, and are prone to all vice?
cards.answer: Indeed we are, except we are regenerated by the Holy Ghost.

cards.question: Doth not God then Injury to Man who in the Law requireth that of him which he is not able to perform?
cards.answer: No; For God had made Man such a one as he might perform it: but Man by the impulsion of the Devil, and his own stubbornness bereaved himself and all his posterity of those Divine Graces.

cards.question: Doth God leave this stubbornness and falling away of Man unpunished?
cards.answer: No: but is angry in most dreadful manner, as well for the sins wherein we are born, as also for those which our selves commit, and in most just Judgment punisheth them with present and everlasting Punishments, as himself pronounceth: Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this Law to do them.

cards.question: Is not God therefore merciful?
cards.answer: Yea, Verily he is merciful; but so, that he is also just: wherefore his Justice requireth that the same which is committed against the divine Majesty of God, should also be recompenced with extream, that is, everlasting Punishment both in Body and Soul.

cards.question: Seeing then by the just Judgment of God we are subject both to temporal and eternal Punishments, is there yet any way or means remaining whereby we may be delivered from these Punishments, and be reconciled to God?
cards.answer: God will have his Justice satisfied: wherefore it is necessary that we satisfy either by our selves, or by another.

cards.question: Are we able to satisfy by our selves?
cards.answer: Not a whit. Nay rather we do every day increase our debt.

cards.question: Is there any creature in Heaven or in Earth, which is only a creature, able to satisfy for us?
cards.answer: None. For first God will not punish that Sin in any other creature which man hath committed: and further, neither can that which is nothing but a creature sustain the wrath of God against sin, and deliver others from it.

cards.question: What manner of Mediatour then, and Deliverer must we seek for?
cards.answer: Such a one verily as is very Man, and perfectly just, and yet in Power above all creatures, that is, one who also is very God.

cards.question: Wherefore is it necessary that he be very Man, and that perfectly just too?
cards.answer: Because that the Justice of God requireth that the same humane nature which hath sinned, do it self likewise make recompence for sin: but he that is himself a sinner, cannot make recompence for others.

cards.question: And who is that Mediatour which is together both very God, and a very perfectly just Man?
cards.answer: Even our Lord Jesus Christ, who is made to us of God’s Wisdom, Righteousness, Sanctification & Redemption.

cards.question: Whence knowest thou this?
cards.answer: Out of the Gospel which God first made known in Paradise, and afterwards did spread it a broad by the Patriarchs and Prophets: shadowed it by Sacrifices and other Ceremonies of the Law; and lastly accomplished it by his only begotten Son Christ our Lord.

cards.question: Is then Salvation restored by Christ to all men who perished in Adam?
cards.answer: Not to all: but to those only who by a true Faith are ingrafted into him, and receive his benefits.

cards.question: Into how many parts is this Creed divided?
cards.answer: Into three: the first of the eternal Father, and our Creation: the second of the Son and our Redemption: the third of the Holy Ghost, and our Sanctification.

cards.question: Seing there is but one only substance of God, why namest thou those three, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost?
cards.answer: Because God hath so manifested himself in his Word, that these three distinct Persons are that one true everlasting God.

cards.question: Why is the Son of God called Jesus, that is, a Saviour?
cards.answer: Because he saveth us from our sins; neither ought any safety to be sought for from any other, nor can elsewhere be found.

cards.question: But why art thou called a Christian?
cards.answer: Because through Faith I am a member of Jesus Christ, and partaker of his anointing, that both I may confess his name, and present my self unto him a lively Sacrifice of thankfulness, and also may in this life fight against Sin and Satan with free and good conscience, and afterwards enjoy an everlasting Kingdom with Christ.

cards.question: For what cause is Christ called the only begotten Son of God, when we also are the Sons of God?
cards.answer: Because Christ alone is the eternal and natural Son of the eternal Father, and we are but Sons adopted of the Father by Grace for his sake.

cards.question: Wherefore callest thou him our Lord?
cards.answer: Because he redeeming and ransoming both our Body and Soul from Sin, not with Gold nor Silver, but with his precious Blood, and delivering us from all the Power of the Devil, hath set us free to serve him.

cards.question: What believest thou when thou sayest, He was conceived by the Holy Ghost, and born of the Virgin Mary?
cards.answer: That the Son of God, who is and continueth true and everlasting God, took the very Nature of man, of the flesh and blood of the Virgin Mary, through the working of the Holy-Ghost, that withal he might be the true Seed of David, like unto his Brethren in all things Sin excepted.

cards.question: What profit takest thou by Christ’s holy Conception and Nativity?
cards.answer: That he is our Mediator, and doth cover with his Innocency and perfect Holiness my Sins, in which I was conceived, that they may not come in the Sight of God.

cards.question: For what cause should he suffer under Pilate, as being his Judg?
cards.answer: That he being innocent and condemned before a civil Judg might deliver us from the severe Judgment of God which remained for all men.

cards.question: Why was it necessary for Christ to humble himself unto death?
cards.answer: Because the Justice and Truth of God could by no other means be satisfied for our sins, but by the very death of the Son of God.

cards.question: But since that Christ died for us, why must we also die?
cards.answer: Our death is not a satisfaction for our Sins, but the abolishing of Sin, and our passage into everlasting Life.

cards.question: What other commodity receive we by the Death of Christ?
cards.answer: That by the virtue of his Death our old man is crucified, slain, and buried together with him, (figured out in holy Baptism) that henceforth evil lusts and desires may not reign in us, but we may offer our selves unto him a Sacrifice of thanksgiving.

cards.question: Why is there added, he descended into Hell?
cards.answer: That in my greatest pains and most grevious temptations I may support my self with this comfort, that my Lord Jesus Christ hath delivered me (by the unspeakable distresses, torments and terrors of his Soul, into which he was plunged both before, and then especially when he hanged on the Cross) from the straits and torments of Hell.
scripture: Matthew 27:46 | Note: Not that he (to wit, Christ

cards.question: What doth the Resurrection of Christ profit us?
cards.answer: First, by his Resurrection he vanquished death, that he might make us partakers of that Righteousness which he had gotten us by his death. Again, we are now also stirred up by his Power to a new Life. Lastly, the Resurrection of our head, Christ, is a Pledge unto us of our glorious Resurrection.

cards.question: How understand you that he ascended into Heaven?
cards.answer: That Christ, his Disciples looking on, was taken up from the Earth into Heaven, and yet still is there for our sakes, and will be until he come again to judge the quick and the dead.

cards.question: Is not Christ with us then until the end of the World, as he hath promised?
cards.answer: Christ is true God, and true Man, and so according to his Manhood is not now on Earth, but according to his Godhead, his Majesty, his Grace, and Spirit is at no time from us.

cards.question: Are not by this means the two natures in Christ pulled assunder, if his Humanity be not wheresoever his Divinity is?
cards.answer: No; for seeing his Divinity is incomprehensible, and every where present, it followeth necessarily that the same is without the bounds of his humane Nature which he took unto him, and yet is nevertheless in it, and abideth personally united to it.

cards.question: Why is it further said, he sitteth at the Right-Hand of God?
cards.answer: Because Christ therefore is ascended into Heaven, to shew there that he is the Head of his Church, by whom the Father governeth all things.

cards.question: What profit is this Glory of our Head Christ unto us?
cards.answer: First, that through his Holy Spirit he poureth upon us his Members heavenly Graces, then that he shieldeth and defendeth us by his Power against all our Enemies.

cards.question: What believest thou concerning the Holy Ghost?
cards.answer: First, that He is true and Coeternal God, with the eternal Father, and the Son; secondly, that he is also given unto me, to make me, through a true Faith, Partaker of Christ and all his Benefits, to comfort me, and to abide with me for ever.

cards.question: What believest thou concerning the Holy and Catholick Church of Christ?
cards.answer: I believe that the Son of God doth from the beginning of the World to the End thereof, gather, defend, and preserve unto himself by his Spirit and Word, out of whole Mankind, a Company chosen to everlasting Life, and agreeing in true Faith; and that I am a lively Member of that Company, and so shal remain for ever.

cards.question: What mean those words, The Communion of Saints?
cards.answer: First, that all and every one who believeth, are in common Partakers of Christ and all his Graces, as being his Members; and then that every one ought readily and chearfully to bestow the Gifts and Graces which they have received to the common Commodity and Safety of all.

cards.question: What believest thou concerning Remission of Sins?
cards.answer: That God, for the Satisfaction made by Christ, hath put out all the Remembrance of my Sins, and also of that Corruption within me wherewith I must fight all my life time, and doth freely indow me with the Righteousness of Christ, that I come not at any time into Judgment.

cards.question: What Comfort hast thou by the Resurrection of the Flesh?
cards.answer: That not only my Soul, after it shall depart out of my Body, shall presently be taken up to Christ, but that this my Flesh also, being raised up by the Power of Christ, shall be again united to my Soul, and shall be made like to the glorious Body of Christ.

cards.question: What Comfort takest thou of the Article of everlasting Life?
cards.answer: That forasmuch as I feel already in my Heart the beginning of everlasting Life, it shall at length come to pass that after this Life I shall enjoy full and perfect Bliss, wherein I may magnify God for ever, which Blessedness verily neither Eye hath seen, nor Ear heard, neither hath any Man in thought conceived it.

cards.question: Why affirmest thou that thou art made Righteous by Faith only?
cards.answer: Not for that I please God through the Worthiness of meer Faith, but because only the Satisfaction, Righteousness and Holiness of Christ is my Righteousness before God, and I cannot take hold of it, or apply it unto my self any other way than by Faith.

cards.question: Why cannot our good Works be Righteousness, or some part of Righteousness before God?
cards.answer: Because that Righteousness which must stand fast before the Judgment of God, must be in all Points perfect and agreeable to the Law of God. Now our Works, even the best of them, are imperfect in this Life, and defiled with Sin.

cards.question: How is it that our good Works merit nothing, seeing God promiseth that he will give a Reward for them both in this Life, and in the Life to come?
cards.answer: That Reward is not given of merit, but of Grace.

cards.question: Seeing then that only Faith maketh us Partakers of Christ and his Benefits, whence doth it proceed?
cards.answer: From the Holy Ghost who kindleth it in our Hearts by the preaching of the Gospel, and other Ordinances, and confirmeth it by the use of the sacraments.

cards.question: Doth then both the Word and sacraments tend to that dnd, as to lead our faith unto the sacrifice of Christ finished on the cross as to the only ground of our salvation?
cards.answer: It is even so; for the Holy Ghost teacheth us by the Gospel, and assureth us by the sacraments, that the salvation of all of us standeth in the only sacrifice of Christ offered for us upon the cross.

cards.question: How many sacraments hath Christ ordained in the new Testament?
cards.answer: Two; Baptism, and the Lord’s Supper.

cards.question: What is Baptism?
cards.answer: Immersion or dipping of the Person in Water in the Name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, by such who are duly qualified by Christ.

cards.question: Who are the proper Subjects of this Ordinance?
cards.answer: Those who do actually profess Repentance towards God, Faith in, and Obedience to our Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.question: Are no Infants to be baptized?
cards.answer: None by no means; for we have neither Precept nor Example for that Practice in all the Book of God.

cards.question: Doth the Scripture any where expressly forbid the Baptizing of Infants?
cards.answer: It is sufficient that the Divine Oracle commands the baptizing of Believers, unless we will make our selves wiser than what is written. Nadab and Abihu were not forbidden to offer strange Fire, yet for so doing they incurred God’s Wrath, because they were commanded to take Fire from the Altar.

cards.question: May not the Infant Seed of Believers under the Gospel be baptized as well as the Infant Seed of Abraham under the Law was circumcised?
cards.answer: No; For Abraham had a Command then from God to circumcise his Infant Seed, but Believers have no Command to baptise their Infants Seed under the Gospel.

cards.question: How art thou admonished and assured in Baptism, that thou art Partaker of the only Sacrifice of Christ?
cards.answer: Because Christ commanded the outward washing of Water, adjoyning this Promise thereunto, that I am no less assuredly washed by his Blood and Spirit from the uncleanness of my Soul, that is, from all my Sins, than I am washed outwardly with Water, whereby all the Filthiness of the Body useth to be purged.

cards.question: Is then the outward Baptism of Water the washing away of Sins?
cards.answer: It is not; for the Blood of Christ alone cleanseth us from all Sin.

cards.question: What Principle of Christ’s Doctrine in the holy Scripture followeth Baptism in order?
cards.answer: Laying on of Hands, as in Hebrews 6:1–2

cards.question: You told us but now, that those who in Confession and Life declare themselves to be Infidels, profane and ungodly, should by the Keys of the Kingdom of Heaven be driven from this Supper: what are the Keys of the Kingdom of Heaven?
cards.answer: Preaching of the Gospel and Ecclesiastical Discipline, by which Heaven is opened to the Believers, and is shut against the Unbelievers.

cards.question: Cannot they then be saved which be unthankful, and remain still careless in their Sins, and are not converted from their Wickedness to God?
cards.answer: By no means; for as the Scripture beareth Witness, neither unchast Persons, nor Idolaters, nor Adulterers, nor Thievs, nor Covetous nor Drunkards, nor Slanderers, nor Robbers, shall enter in to the Kingdom of God.

cards.question: Of what Parts consisteth the Conversion of Man unto God?
cards.answer: It consisteth of the mortifying of the old Man, and a quickning of the new Man.

cards.question: What is the mortifying of the old Man?
cards.answer: To be truly and heartily sorry that thou hast offended God by thy Sins, and daily more and more hate and eschew them.

cards.question: What is the quickning of the new Man?
cards.answer: True Joy in God through Christ, and an earnest Desire to order thy Life according to God’s Will and to do all good Works.

cards.question: What are good Works?
cards.answer: Those only which are done by a true Faith, according to God’s Law, and are referred only to his Glory, and not those which are imagined by us as seeming to us to be right and good, or which are delivered and commanded by Men.

cards.question: Which is the Law of God?
cards.answer: The Decalogue, or ten Commandments.

cards.question: How are these Commandments divided?
cards.answer: Into two Tables, whereof the former delivereth in four Commandments, how we ought to behave our selves towards God: the latter delivereth in six Commandments, what duties we owe unto our Neighbours.

cards.question: What is the Preface to the ten Commandments?
cards.answer: I am JEHOVAH, the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the Land of Egypt, out of the House of Bondage.

cards.question: What is the first Commandment?
cards.answer: Thou shalt have no other Gods before me.

cards.question: What is Idolatry?
cards.answer: It is in Place of that one God, or besides that one true God who hath manifested himself in his Word and Works, to make or imagin, and account any other thing wherein thou reposest thy Hope and Confidence.

cards.question: What doth this second Commandment require?
cards.answer: That we should not express or represent God by any Image or shape and figure, or worship him any otherwise then he hath commanded himself in his Word to be worshipped.

cards.question: May there then at all any Images or Resemblances of things be made?
cards.answer: God neither ought, nor can be represented by any means: and for the Creatures, although it be lawful to express them, yet God forbiddeth notwithstanding their Images to be made or had, as thereby to worship or honour either them, or God by them:

cards.question: But may not Images be tolerated in Churches, which may serve for Books unto the common People?
cards.answer: No, for ’tis not seemly that we should be wiser then God, who will have his Church to be taught by the lively preaching of his Word, and not with dumb Images.

cards.question: What is the third Commandment?
cards.answer: Thou shalt not take the Name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his Name in vain.

cards.question: Is it then so grievous a Sin by swearing, or banning, to take the Name of God in vain, as that God is also angry with them who in as much as in them lieth do not forbid or hinder it?
cards.answer: Surely most grievous: for neither is there any Sin greater, or more offending God, than the despiting of his sacred Name; wherefore also he would have this Sin to be punished with Death.

cards.question: Is it lawful to swear by Saints, or other Creatures?
cards.answer: No, for a lawful Oath is an Invocation of God, whereby we desire that he, as the only searcher of Hearts, bear Witness unto the Truth, and will punish the Swearer if he wittingly swear falsely: but this Honour agreeth to no Creature.

cards.question: What is the fifth Commandment?
cards.answer: Honour thy Father and Mother, that thy dayes may be long in the Land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

cards.question: What is the sixth Commandment?
cards.answer: Thou shalt do no Murder.

cards.question: What is the seventh Commandment?
cards.answer: Thou shalt not commit Adultery.

cards.question: What is the meaning of the seventh Commandment?
cards.answer: That God hath in Execration all Turpitude and Filthiness, and therefore we also must utterly hate, and detest it, and contrary-wife, live temperately, modestly, and chastly, whether we live in holy Wedlock, or in single life.

cards.question: Forbiddeth God nothing else in this Commandment but actual Adultery, and such kinds of uncleanness?
cards.answer: Yea, for seeing both our Body and Soul are the Temples of the Holy Ghost, God will have us to possess both in Purity and Holiness, and therefore Deeds, Gestures, Words, Thoughts, filthy Lusts, and whatsoever inticeth a Man unto these, all these God wholly forbiddeth.

cards.question: What is the eighth Commandment?
cards.answer: Thou shalt not steal.

cards.question: What is the ninth Commandment?
cards.answer: Thou shalt not bear false Witness against thy Neighbour.

cards.question: What is the tenth Commandment?
cards.answer: Thou shalt not covet thy Neighbours House, nor his Wife, nor his Servant, nor his Maid, nor his Ox, nor his Ass, nor any thing that is his.

cards.question: What doth the tenth Commandment forbid?
cards.answer: That our Hearts be not at any time moved by the least Desire or Cogitation against any Commandment of God, but that continually and from our Heart we detest all Sin, and contrarily delight in all Righteousness.

cards.question: But can they who are converted to God, perfectly observe, and keep these Commandments?
cards.answer: No, but even the holiest Men as long they live, have only small Beginnings of this Obedience, yet so that they begin with an unfeigned and earnest desire and endeavour to live not according to some only, but according to all the Commandments of God.

cards.question: Wherefore is Prayer necessary for Christians?
cards.answer: Because it is the chief part of that thankfulness which God requireth of us, and also because God giveth them only his Grace and Holy Spirit, who with unfeigned gronings beg them continually of him and yeild him thanks for them.

cards.question: Why is that added, which art in Heaven?
cards.answer: That we conceive not basely nor terrenely of God’s Heavenly Majesty, and also that we look for, and expect from his Omnipotency whatsoever things are necessary for our Soul and Body.

cards.question: What meaneth this Particle, Amen?
cards.answer: That the thing is sure, and out of doubt: for my Prayer is much more certainly heard of God, than I feel in my Heart that I unfeignedly desire the same.

cards.question: What is the chief end of human life?
cards.answer: To know God.

cards.question: What is the true and right knowledge of God?
cards.answer: When we know Him in order that we may honour Him.

cards.question: How do we honour Him aright?
cards.answer: We put our reliance on Him, by serving Him in obedience to His will, by calling upon Him in all our need, seeking salvation and every good thing in Him, and acknowledging with heart and mouth that all our good proceeds from Him.

cards.question: Since there is but one God, why do you mention the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, who are three?
cards.answer: Because in the one essence of God, we have to look on the Father as the beginning and origin, and the first cause of all things; then the Son, who is Eternal Wisdom; and the Holy Spirit who is His virtue and power shed abroad over all creatures, but still perpetually resident in Himself.

cards.question: Why do you call Him Father?
cards.answer: It is with reference to Christ who is His eternal Word, begotten of Him before time, and being sent into this world was demonstrated and declared to be His Son. But since God is the Father of Jesus Christ, it follows that He is our Father also.

cards.question: In what sense do you mean that He is Almighty?
cards.answer: That does not mean that He has a power which He does not exercise, but that He disposes all things by His Providence, governs the world by His will, ruling all as it seems good to Him.

cards.question: Why do you add that He is Creator of heaven and earth?
cards.answer: Because He has manifested Himself to us by works [Ps 104; Rom 1:20] we ought to seek Him in them. Our mind cannot comprehend His essence. But the world is for us like a mirror in which we may contemplate Him in so far as it is expedient for us to know Him.

cards.question: What is the meaning of the name Jesus which you give to Him?
cards.answer: It means Saviour, and was given to Him by the angel at the command of God (Mat 1:21).

cards.question: What, next, is meant by the name of Christ?
cards.answer: By this title His office is still better expressed—for it signifies that He was appointed by the Father to be ordained King, Priest, and Prophet.

cards.question: In what sense do you call Christ a Prophet?
cards.answer: Because on coming down into the world (Isa 7:14) He was the sovereign messenger and ambassador of God His Father, to give full exposition of God’s will toward the world and so put an end to all prophecies and revelations (Heb 1:2).

cards.question: What does His Kingdom minister to us?
cards.answer: By it, we are set at liberty in our conscience and are filled with His spiritual riches in order to live in righteousness and holiness, and we are also armed with power to overcome the devil, the flesh, and the world—the enemies of our souls.

cards.question: How is He “our Lord”?
cards.answer: Because He is appointed by the Father to have us under His government, to administer the Kingdom and the Lordship of God in heaven and on earth, and to be the Head of men and believers (Eph 5:23; Col 1:18).

cards.question: What do you mean by the two clauses, “Conceived of the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary”?
cards.answer: That He was formed in womb of the Virgin Mary, of her proper substance, to be the seed of David, as had been foretold (Ps 132:11), and yet that this was wrought by the miraculous operation of the Holy Spirit, without the cooperation of a man (Mat 1:18; Luke 1:35).

cards.question: Was it then required that He should put on our very flesh?
cards.answer: Yes, because it was necessary that the disobedience committed by man against God should be redressed in human nature. And moreover He could not otherwise be our Mediator to reconcile us to God His Father (1Ti 2:5; Heb 4:15).

cards.question: Why do you go immediately from His birth to His death, passing over the whole history of His life?
cards.answer: Because nothing is said here about what belongs properly to the substance of our redemption.

cards.question: Is there greater importance in His having been crucified than if He had been put death in another way?
cards.answer: Yes, as Paul also shows us when he says that He hanged on a tree to take our curse upon Himself and acquit us of it (Gal 3:13). For that kind of death was accursed of God (Deu 21:23).

cards.question: What is the meaning of the additional clause: “He descended into hell”?
cards.answer: That He not only suffered natural death, which is the separation of the body from the soul, but also that His soul was pierced with amazing anguish, which St. Peter calls the pains of death (Acts 2:24).

cards.question: But since He is God Himself, how could He be in such dread, as if He were forsaken by God?
cards.answer: We must hold that it was according to His human nature that He was in that extremity: and that in order to allow this, His Deity held itself back a little, as if concealed, that is, did not how its power.

cards.question: How is it possible that Jesus Christ, who is the salvation of the world, should have been under such damnation?
cards.answer: He was not to remain under it. For though He experienced the horror we have spoken of, He was by no means oppressed by it. On the contrary, He battled with the power of hell, to break and destroy it.

cards.question: Did He ascend in such a way that He is no longer on earth?
cards.answer: Yes. For after He had performed all that He was enjoined by the Father, and was required for our salvation, there was no need for Him to remain on earth.

cards.question: But did Christ in going to heaven withdraw from us, in such a way that He has now ceased to be with us?
cards.answer: No. On the contrary, He has promised that He will be with us to the end (Mat 28:20).

cards.question: Is it in bodily presence that He remains with us?
cards.answer: No, for it is one thing to speak of His body which was taken up into heaven, and another to speak of His power, which is spread abroad everywhere (Luke 24:51; Acts 2:33).

cards.question: How do you understand that He “sitteth on the right hand of the Father”?
cards.answer: It means that He has received the dominion of heaven and earth, so that He reigns and rules over all (Mat 28:18).

cards.question: But what is meant by “right hand”, and by “sitteth”?
cards.answer: It is a similitude taken from earthly princes, who are wont to place on their right hand those whom they make their lieutenants to govern in their name.

cards.question: Does the fact that Christ is to come gain to judge the world bring us any consolation?
cards.answer: Yes, indeed. For we are certain that He will appear only for our salvation.

cards.question: We should not then fear the last judgment, and have a horror of it?
cards.answer: No, since we are not to come before any other judge then He who is our Advocate, and who has taken our cause in hand to defend us.

cards.question: What is the Catholic Church?
cards.answer: The community of the faithful which God has ordained and elected to eternal life.

cards.question: In what sense do you call the Church holy?
cards.answer: All whom God has chosen He justifies, and reforms to holiness and innocence, that His glory may be reflected in them (Rom 8:30). And so Jesus Christ sanctified the Church which He redeemed, that it might be glorious and without blemish (Eph 5:25-27).

cards.question: What is meant by the word Catholic or Universal?
cards.answer: It is meant to signify, that there is only one Head of the faithful, so they must all be united in one body, so that there are not several churches but one only, which is extended throughout the whole world (Eph 4:15; 1Co 12:12,27).

cards.question: But is this holiness which you attribute to the Church already perfect?
cards.answer: Not as long as she battles in this world, for elements of imperfection always remain and will never be entirely removed, until she is united completely to Jesus Christ her Head, by whom she is sanctified.

cards.question: Can this Church be known in any other way than by believing in her?
cards.answer: There is indeed the visible Church of God, for the recognition of which He has certain signs, but here we speak properly of the fellowship of those whom He has elected to salvation which cannot be seen plainly by the eye.

cards.question: What do you understand by this word “forgiveness”?
cards.answer: That God by His pure goodness forgives and pardons the sins of believers, so that they are not brought to account before His judgment, in order to be punished.

cards.question: And so outside the Church there is nothing but damnation and death?
cards.answer: Certainly, for all those who separate themselves from the community of the faithful to form a sect on its own, have no hope of salvation so long as they are in schism.

cards.question: How will this resurrection take place?
cards.answer: Those who were formerly dead will resume their bodies, but with another quality; that is, they will no longer be subject to death or corruption, even although their substance will remain the same. Those who will survive God will miraculously raise up through a sudden change, as it is said (1Co 15:52).

cards.question: Will this resurrection not be common to the evil and the good?
cards.answer: Yes indeed, but not in the same way. Some will rise to salvation and joy, others to condemnation and death (John 5:29; Mat 25:46).

cards.question: Since we have the foundation on which faith is laid, we should be quite able to gather from it what true faith is?
cards.answer: Yes, indeed, It is a sure and steadfast knowledge of the love of God toward us, according as He declares in His gospel that He is our Father and Saviour (through the mediation of Jesus Christ).

cards.question: What good comes to us from this faith, when we have it?
cards.answer: It justifies us before God, and makes us obtain eternal life.

cards.question: How so Is not man justified by good works in a holy life and in conformity to God?
cards.answer: If any one be found so perfect, he might well be deemed righteous, but since we are all poor sinners, we must look elsewhere for a worthiness in which to make answer before the judgment of God.

cards.question: But are all our works so reprobate that they cannot merit grace before?
cards.answer: God First, all that we do of ourselves, by our own nature, is vicious, and therefore cannot please God. He condemns them all.

cards.question: What do you mean then by saying that a man is justified by faith?
cards.answer: That in believing the promises of the gospel and in receiving them in true affiance of the heart, we enter into this righteousness.

cards.question: But after God has once received us, are the works which we do by His grace, not pleasing to Him?
cards.answer: Yes, they are, in that He generously accepts them, not however in virtue of their own worthiness.

cards.question: But can we say from this that a Christian man is justified by works after God has called him, or that through them he merits the love of God, and so obtains eternal life?
cards.answer: No. On the contrary, it is said that no man living will be justified in His sight (Ps 143:2). Therefore we have to pray that He will not enter into judgment with us, nor call us to account.

cards.question: You do not mean therefore that the good works of believers are useless?
cards.answer: No. For God promises to reward them fully, both in this world and in Paradise. But this comes from His gratuitous love toward us: moreover He buries all our faults, so as never to remember them.

cards.question: Faith, then, not only does not make us careless of good works, but is the root from which they are produced?
cards.answer: It is so, and for this reason, the doctrine of the Gospel is comprehended in these two points, faith and repentance.

cards.question: What is repentance?
cards.answer: Dissatisfaction with and a hatred of evil and a love good proceeding from the fear of God, and inducing us to mortify our flesh, so that we may be governed and led by the Holy Spirit, in the service of God.

cards.question: What rule has He given us by which we may direct our life?
cards.answer: His law.

cards.question: What is the content of the first table?
cards.answer: The Way of the true worship of God.

cards.question: And what does He require briefly in this first commandment?
cards.answer: That we reserve for Him alone the honour that belongs to Him, and do not transfer it elsewhere.

cards.question: What is the honour due Him?
cards.answer: To adore Him alone, to call upon Him, to have our affiance in Him, and all similar things due to His majesty.

cards.question: Does He entirely forbid us to make any image?
cards.answer: No, but He forbids us to make any image with which to represent God, or to worship Him.

cards.question: Why is it unlawful to represent God visibly?
cards.answer: Because there is no resemblance between Him who is eternal Spirit and incomprehensible, and corporal, dead, corruptible and visible matter (Deu 4:15; Isa 40:7; Rom 1:23; Acts 17:24-25).

cards.question: How is this to be understood, that He punishes the sin of the fathers on their children?
cards.answer: To give us a greater fear of Him. He says not only that He will inflict punishment on those who offend Him, but that their offspring also will be cursed after them.

cards.question: Does He mean that the obedience of a faithful man will save the whole of his race, even if they are still wicked?
cards.answer: No, but that He will extend His goodness toward the faithful to such an extent, that in love for them He will make Himself know to their children, not only to prosper them according to the flesh, but to sanctify them by His Spirit, that He might make them obedient to His will.

cards.question: Can the name of God we used lawfully in oaths?
cards.answer: Yes, when they are necessary, i.e., in order to uphold the truth, when it requires it, and in maintaining love and concord among us.

cards.question: Does He order us to labour six days a week that may rest on the seventh?
cards.answer: Not precisely, but in allowing us to labour for six days, He excepts the seventh, on which it is not right to be engaged in work.

cards.question: What is this spiritual rest?
cards.answer: It is to cease from our own works, that the Lord may work in us.

cards.question: But why is the seventh day appointed rather than any other day?
cards.answer: The number seven implies perfection in Scripture. Thus it is suited to denote perpetuity. It reminds us also that our spiritual rest is only begun in this life, and will not be perfect until we depart from this world.

cards.question: Must we meditate continually on the works of God, or is it sufficient on one day out of seven?
cards.answer: We must do it every hour, but because of our weakness, one day is specially appointed. And this is the polity of which I spoke.

cards.question: What do you mean by “honour”?
cards.answer: That children be humble and obedient toward their parents, doing them honour and reverence, helping them and being at their command, as they are bound.

cards.question: Seeing this life is full of misery, why does God promise man as a favour that he will live long?
cards.answer: However miserable it may be, life on earth is a blessing from God to the faithful, if only for this reason, that in it God testifies to His fatherly love in supporting them in it.

cards.question: Does it follow conversely, that the man who dies prematurely is cursed of God?
cards.answer: By no means. Rather does it sometimes happen that the Lord withdraws from this world more quickly those whom He loves most.

cards.question: What of those who are rebellious against their father and mother?
cards.answer: Not only will God punish them at the last judgment, but here also God will exercise judgment on their bodies, it may be by letting them die before their time, or ignominiously, or in some other way.

cards.question: Is it sufficient for us not to hate or to bear ill will?
cards.answer: No, for in condemning hatred God signifies that He requires us to love our neighbours and seek their salvation, and all this with true affection and without simulation.

cards.question: What is the ninth commandment?
cards.answer: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.

cards.question: Can we now give a short summary of the whole law?
cards.answer: We can, reducing it to two articles—the first of which is that we are to love God with all our heart, and with all our soul, and with all our strength; the second that we love our neighbours as ourselves.

cards.question: What is meant by the love of God?
cards.answer: To love Him as God is to have and hold Him as Lord, Saviour and Father, and this requires reverence, honour, faith, and obedience along with love.

cards.question: What does “with all our heart” signify, and “with all our soul, and with all our strength”?
cards.answer: Such a zeal and such a vehemence, that there is in us no desire, no will, no intention and no thought, contrary to this love.

cards.question: What do you understand by “our neighbours”?
cards.answer: Not only our parents and friends, or those acquainted with us, but also those who are unknown to us, and even our enemies.

cards.question: Seeing that the law of God comprises the form of worshiping Him aright, should not the Christian man live according to its command?
cards.answer: Yes indeed. But there is some infirmity in us, so that no man acquits himself perfectly in it.

cards.question: Why then does the Lord require a perfection which is beyond our ability?
cards.answer: He requires nothing which we are not bound to perform. Nevertheless, provided we take care to conform our life to what we are told here, although we are very far from reaching perfection, the Lord does not impute our faults to us.

cards.question: Do we not have perfect rule of goodness in the Law?
cards.answer: Yes, and therefore God demands nothing from us, but to follow it; and, on the other hand, repudiates and rejects all that a man undertakes to do beyond what it contains. The only sacrifice He requires is obedience (1Sa 15:22; Jer 7:21-23).

cards.question: Do you think that He alone is to be invoked?
cards.answer: Yes, for He requires this as the worship proper to His Deity.

cards.question: Nevertheless, should we not give thanks to men for the kindness which they do to us?
cards.answer: Certainly, if only for the reason that God honours them by communicating His blessings to us through their hands, for in this way He lays us under obligation to Him, and wishes us to be mindful of them.

cards.question: Let us now speak of the way of prayer to God. Is it sufficient to pray with the tongue, or does prayer require also the spirit and the heart?
cards.answer: The tongue is not always necessary, but there must be understanding and affection.

cards.question: All prayers, then, made only with the mouth are vain?
cards.answer: Not only vain, but also displeasing to God.

cards.question: What kind of affection should we have in prayer?
cards.answer: First, that we feel our misery and poverty, and that this feeling should beget sorrow and anguish in us. Secondly, that we have an earnest desire to obtain grace from God. This desire will also kindle our hearts, and engender in us an ardent longing to pray.

cards.question: And what of those who doubt, not knowing if God hears or not?
cards.answer: Their prayers are utterly void, since they have no promise, for He says that whatever we ask, believing, we shall receive (Mat 21:22; Mark 11:24).

cards.question: Do you understand that we are to call upon God only, in the Name of Jesus Christ?
cards.answer: I understand so, for we have an express commandment about this. And in it we are promised that by His intercession our requests will be heard (John 14:13).

cards.question: Shall we then dare to go to God familiarly, as a child to his father?
cards.answer: Yes, in fact with greater assurance of obtaining what we ask. For if we, being evil, cannot refuse our children bread and meat, when they ask, how much less will our heavenly Father, who is not only good, but sovereign goodness itself (Mat 7:11).

cards.question: Why do you not call God your God, but call Him our Father together?
cards.answer: Each believer may indeed call Him his own Father, but in this formula Jesus Christ instructs us to pray together, to remind us that in our prayers we are to exercise charity towards our neighbours, and not only to care for ourselves.

cards.question: What is meant by the clause “who art in heaven”?
cards.answer: It is just the same as if I were to call Him exalted, mighty, incomprehensible.

cards.question: Do you think that His glory can increase or decrease?
cards.answer: Not in itself. But this means that it may be manifested, as it ought to be, that all the works which God performs may appear glorious, as indeed they are, so that He Himself may be glorified in every way.

cards.question: What do you understand by the Kingdom of God in the second petition?
cards.answer: It consists principally of two things: that He leads His own, and governs them by His Spirit, and on the other hand casts down and confounds the reprobate who refuse to subject themselves to His rule, and so makes it clear that there is no power which can resist His power.

cards.question: What do you mean by asking that the will of God may be done?
cards.answer: That all creatures may be brought under obedience to Him, and so that everything may be done according to His good will.

cards.question: Do you mean that nothing can be done contrary to His will?
cards.answer: We ask not only that He may bring all things to pass, as He has determined in His counsel, but also that, putting down all rebellion, He may bring all wills to conform to His own.

cards.question: Why do you add “on earth as it is in heaven”?
cards.answer: Since His heavenly creatures or His angels have it as their own object to obey Him, promptly without opposition, we desire that the same thing may be done on earth, that is, that all men may yield themselves in voluntary obedience.

cards.question: Why do you say “daily” and “this day”?
cards.answer: That we may learn to be content, and not to covet more than our need requires.

cards.question: Since this prayer is common to all, how can the rich, who have an abundance of good things, provide for a long time, ask for bread each day?
cards.answer: The rich, as well as the poor, should understand that none of the things profit them, unless the Lord grant them the use of them, and by His grace make it profitable to them. Thus in having we have nothing, unless He gives it to us.

cards.question: What does the fifth petition contain?
cards.answer: That it pleases God to pardon our sins.

cards.question: How do you think that such remission is granted to us?
cards.answer: As the words of Jesus Christ used declare: because our sins are debts, making us liable to eternal death, we pray that God will pardon us out of His sheer kindness.

cards.question: You mean, them, that it is by the gratuitous goodness of God that we obtain remission of sins?
cards.answer: Yes, for we can offer no satisfaction for the smallest sin we commit, if God does no exercise His sheer kindness toward us in forgiving us them all.

cards.question: What gain and profit do we receive, when God pardons our sins?
cards.answer: We are acceptable to Him, just as if we were righteous and innocent, and our consciences are assured of His paternal love, from which comes salvation and life.

cards.question: What does the word “temptation” signify?
cards.answer: The wiles and assaults of the devil, which he uses to attack us, seeing that our natural judgment is prone to be deceived and to deceive us, and our will is always ready to addict itself to evil rather than to good.

cards.question: What is intended by the addition, “For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever”?
cards.answer: To remind us again that our prayers are altogether grounded on the power and goodness of God, and not on ourselves, for we are not worthy to open our mouth in prayer; and also that we may learn to close our prayers in His praise.

cards.question: Where do you find this Word?
cards.answer: It is comprised for us in the Holy Scriptures.

cards.question: Is it necessary, then, that there should be pastors?
cards.answer: Yes; and that we should hear them, receiving the teaching of the Lord in humility by their mouth. Therefore whoever despises them and refuses to hear them, rejects Jesus Christ, and separates himself from the fellowship of the faithful (Mat 10:40; Luke 10:16).

cards.question: Is there no other means than the Word by which God communicates Himself to us?
cards.answer: To the preaching of His Word He has conjoined the sacraments.

cards.question: What is a sacrament?
cards.answer: An outward attestation of the grace of God which, by a visible sign, represents spiritual things to imprint the promises of God more firmly in our hearts, and to make us more sure of them.

cards.question: Does a visible and natural sign have this power to assure the conscience?
cards.answer: No, not of itself, but in so far as it is ordained of God for this end.

cards.question: But what assurance of grace can the sacraments give, seeing that good and bad both receive them?
cards.answer: Although the unbelievers and the wicked make of none effect the grace offered them through the sacraments, yet it does not follow that the proper nature of the sacraments is also made of non effect.

cards.question: How, then, and when do the sacraments produce this effect?
cards.answer: When we receive them in faith, seeking Jesus Christ alone and His grace in them.

cards.question: How many sacraments are there in the Christian Church?
cards.answer: There are only two sacraments common to all which the Lord Jesus has instituted for the whole company of the faithful.

cards.question: What likeness and difference is there between them?
cards.answer: Baptism is for us a kind of entrance into the Church of God, for it testifies that instead of our being strangers to Him, God receives us as members of His family. The Supper testifies that God as a good Father carefully feeds and refreshes the members of His household.

cards.question: You do not mean that the water is a washing of the soul?
cards.answer: By no means, for that pertains to the blood of Christ alone, which was shed in order to wipe away all our stains and render us pure and unpolluted before God (I John 1:7; I Peter 1:19). This is fulfilled in us when our consciences are sprinkled by the Holy Spirit. But by the sacrament that is sealed to us.

cards.question: Do you think that the water is only a figure to us?
cards.answer: It is such a figure that the reality is conjoined with it, for God does not promise us anything in vain. Accordingly it is certain that in baptism the forgiveness of sins is offered to us and we receive it.

cards.question: How is this grace applied to us in baptism?
cards.answer: In it we are clothed with Jesus Christ, and receive His Spirit, provided that we do not make ourselves unworthy of the promises given to us in it.

cards.question: What is the proper use of baptism on our part?
cards.answer: It consists in faith and in repentance. That is, assurance that we have our spiritual purity in Christ, and in feeling within us, and declaring to our neighbours by our works, that His Spirit dwells in us to mortify our natural desires and bring us to follow the will of God.

cards.question: On what conditions should we baptize little children?
cards.answer: As a sign and testimony that they are heirs of God’s blessing promised to the seed of the faithful, that when they come of age they are to acknowledge the truth of their baptism, in order to derive benefit from it.

cards.question: But why does the Lord represent His body by the bread and His blood by the wine?
cards.answer: To signify that as it is the particular virtue of bread to nourish our bodies, to refresh and sustain us in this mortal life, so it pertains to His body to act toward our souls, i.e., in nourishing and quickening them spiritually, so His blood is our joy, our refreshing and our spiritual strength.

cards.question: Do you mean that we must truly communicate in the body and blood of the Lord?
cards.answer: I understand so. But since the whole affiance of our salvation rests in the obedience which He has rendered to God, His Father, in order that it may be imputed to us as if it were ours, we must possess Him: for His blessings are not ours, unless He gives Himself to us first.

cards.question: Is not the way to receive Him by faith?
cards.answer: Yes. Not only in believing that He died and rose again, in order to deliver us from eternal death, and acquire life for us, but also that He dwells in us, and conjoined with us in a union as the Head with the members, that by virtue of this conjunction He may make us partakers of all His grace.

cards.question: What is the blessing that we have in the sacrament, and what more does it minister to us?
cards.answer: This communion is more abundantly confirmed in us, ratified as it were, for although Jesus Christ is truly communicated to us both by baptism and by the Gospel, nevertheless this only in part, and not fully.

cards.question: What then fully do we have through the sign of the bread?
cards.answer: That the body of the Lord Jesus which was once offered to reconcile us to God, is now given to us, to certify to us that we have part in this reconciliation.

cards.question: What do we have in the sign of the wine?
cards.answer: That the Lord Jesus, who once shed His blood in payment and satisfaction for our offences, gives it to us to drink, that we may have no doubt at all of receiving its fruit.

cards.question: The Supper, then, was not instituted in order to offer up the body of Jesus the Son to the Father?
cards.answer: No, for this office pertains to none but Him alone, since He is the eternal Priest (Heb 5:5). But He commands us only to receive His body, not to offer it (Mat 26:26).

cards.question: Why is there a double sign?
cards.answer: Our Lord has appointed it for the sake of our weakness, in order to teach us that He is not only food to our souls, but drink also, so that we may seek our nourishment wholly and entirely in Him, and not elsewhere.

cards.question: Should all men equally use the second sign, that is the chalice?
cards.answer: Yes, this is according to the commandment of Jesus Christ, against which nothing is to be attempted.

cards.question: But how can this be, when the body of Jesus Christ is in heaven, and we are pilgrims on this earth?
cards.answer: By the incomprehensible power of His Spirit, who conjoins things separated by distance.

cards.question: What is the right use of this sacrament?
cards.answer: That which St. Paul declares, namely that a man examine himself before he approach to it (1Co 11:28).

cards.question: To whom does it belong truly to baptize and administer the Supper?
cards.answer: To those who are publicly charged to teach in the Church. For the preaching of the Word and the distribution of the sacraments are things conjoined.
